sk: द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति ||
ro: dvā · suparṇā · sayujā · sakhāyā · samānaṁ · vṛkṣaṁ · pariṣasvajāte · tayoḥ · anyaḥ · pippalaṁ · svādu · atti · anaśnan · anyaḥ · abhicākaśīti ||
hi: दो (द्वा) सुपर्ण (beautiful-winged birds / सुन्दर पंखों वाले पक्षी), सयुजा (inseparably united / सदा संयुक्त), सखाया (friends / companions / सखा) — समान वृक्ष (the same tree / एक ही वृक्ष) को परिषस्वजाते (have embraced / आलिंगन किए हुए हैं)। उन दोनों में से एक (अन्यः) पिप्पल (the fruit / फल) को स्वादु अत्ति (eats with relish / स्वाद ले-लेकर खाता है); दूसरा (अन्यः) अनश्नन् (not eating / बिना खाए) अभिचाकशीति (simply looks on / केवल देखता रहता है)।
en: Two birds (dvā suparṇā), inseparably united (sayujā), companions (sakhāyā), have embraced (pariṣasvajāte) the same tree (samānaṁ vṛkṣam). Of the two, one (anyaḥ) eats the sweet fruit (pippalaṁ svādu atti); the other (anyaḥ), not eating (anaśnan), simply looks on (abhicākaśīti).

ws.h: सदा संयुक्त / अविभाज्य रूप से जुड़े
आलिंगन किए हुए हैं / लिपटे हुए हैं
केवल देखता रहता है / गहन दृष्टि से निहारता है

gr:
व्याकरण: द्वा सुपर्णा — 'द्वा' = द्विवचन (dual) 'दो'; 'सुपर्णा' = सु (सुन्दर) + पर्ण (पंख) — 'सुन्दर पंखों वाले पक्षी।' सयुजा सखाया — 'सयुजा' = सम् + युज् (जोड़ना) — 'सदा संयुक्त'; 'सखाया' = सखि (मित्र) का द्विवचन। समानं वृक्षम् — 'समानम्' = एक ही; 'वृक्षम्' = शरीर / संसार-वृक्ष — दोनों पक्षी एक ही वृक्ष पर बैठे हैं। परिषस्वजाते — परि + स्वज् (आलिंगन करना) — 'लिपटे हुए हैं' — दोनों वृक्ष से अभिन्न। तयोः अन्यः = 'उन दोनों में एक'; पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्ति = 'फल को स्वाद ले-लेकर खाता है' — जीवात्मा कर्मफल भोगता है। अनश्नन् = अन् + अश् (खाना) — 'बिना खाए' — साक्षी कर्मफल से अस्पृष्ट। अभिचाकशीति = अभि + √चक्ष् का यङ्लुक् (intensive/frequentative) — 'गहनता से निरन्तर देखता है' — साक्षी निष्क्रिय नहीं, सतत जागरूक। दो पक्षियों का रूपक — उपनिषदों का सर्वाधिक प्रसिद्ध रूपक: (1) खाने वाला पक्षी = जीवात्मा — सुख-दुःख भोगता; (2) देखने वाला पक्षी = परमात्मा / साक्षी — सदा शान्त, अस्पृष्ट। यह मन्त्र ऋग्वेद (1.164.20) में सर्वप्रथम आता है।
Eng: The two birds — the Upanishads' most famous parable. 'Dvā suparṇā' = two beautiful-winged birds. 'Sayujā sakhāyā' = inseparably united friends. 'Pariṣasvajāte' = have embraced the same tree (= body/saṁsāra). One bird eats the fruit (jīva experiencing karma-fruits); the other watches without eating (ātman/witness). 'Abhicākaśīti' is the yaṅ-luk intensive of √cakṣ — 'gazes intensely/continuously,' not mere casual seeing.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — दो पक्षी = (1) जीवात्मा — अज्ञान-वश कर्मफल (fruits of karma) खाता है — सुख-दुःख भोगता है। (2) परमात्मा / साक्षी-चैतन्य (witness-consciousness) — अनश्नन् (non-eating) — कर्मफल से अस्पृष्ट (untouched)। 'सयुजा सखाया' = दोनों सदा एक साथ — किन्तु एक (जीव) अज्ञान से ग्रस्त, दूसरा (ब्रह्म) सदा मुक्त।
advaita.en: Shankara says two birds = (1) the jīvātmā — eats the fruits of karma due to ignorance — experiences pleasure and pain. (2) Paramātmā / witness-consciousness — anaśnan (not eating) — untouched by karma-fruit. 'Sayujā sakhāyā' = both always together — but one (jīva) is bound by ignorance, the other (Brahman) is ever free.
advaita.ins: You are two birds sitting on one tree. One bird is you-as-you-think-you-are — eating the fruits of life, sometimes sweet, sometimes bitter, always wanting more. The other bird is you-as-you-really-are — the witness, the one who simply watches, untouched, at peace. The tragedy is that the eating bird has forgotten the watching bird. The liberation is remembering.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — दो पक्षी = (1) जीवात्मा — कर्मफल भोगने वाला — भगवान् से भिन्न (distinct) किन्तु अभिन्न (inseparable)। (2) भगवान् / अन्तर्यामी (inner controller) — अनश्नन् — कर्मफल नहीं भोगता — जीव का मार्गदर्शक (guide) और सखा (friend)। 'सखाया' = भगवान् जीव के सखा (friend/companion) हैं — स्वामी-भृत्य नहीं।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says two birds = (1) the jīvātmā — the enjoyer of karma-fruits — distinct from God but inseparable. (2) God / antaryāmī (inner controller) — anaśnan — does not enjoy karma-fruits — the guide and friend of the jīva. 'Sakhāyā' = God is the jīva's friend/companion — not master-servant.
vishisht.ins: Two birds, one tree. You're one bird — eating the fruits of your life, tasting sweetness and bitterness. God is the other bird — your companion, your friend, sitting right next to you, watching. He doesn't eat your karma. He watches, guides, loves. He's been with you since the beginning — on every tree, in every life.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — दो पक्षी = (1) मनोमय पुरुष (mental being) — संसार-वृक्ष (tree of world-existence) पर कर्मफल भोगता है। (2) अन्तरात्मा / psychic being — शुद्ध चेतना (pure consciousness) — साक्षी (witness) — अभिचाकशीति = 'intensely gazes' = चेतना सदा जागरूक (ever-aware)। दोनों एक ही अस्तित्व (existence) के दो पक्ष (aspects)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says two birds = (1) the mental being — enjoys the fruits on the tree of world-existence. (2) the inner Self / psychic being — pure consciousness — the witness — abhicākaśīti = 'intensely gazes' = consciousness ever-aware. Both are two aspects of one existence.
aurobindo.ins: Two aspects of you sit on the tree of your life. One eats — tasting every experience, sweet and bitter, always involved. The other watches — intensely aware, never eating, never losing itself. The eating is necessary — it's how consciousness explores the world. But the watching is what you fundamentally are.

dp.q: 🔍 The two birds — origin, meaning, and impact
dp.a:
यह दो पक्षियों का रूपक भारतीय दर्शन की सर्वाधिक प्राचीन, प्रसिद्ध और सर्वाधिक उद्धृत छवियों में से एक है। उत्पत्ति: यह मन्त्र सर्वप्रथम ऋग्वेद (1.164.20) में दीर्घतमस् ऋषि द्वारा रचित मिलता है — सम्भवतः 1500-1200 ई.पू. — मानव इतिहास की प्राचीनतम दार्शनिक ऋचाओं में से एक। श्वेताश्वतर (4.6) भी इसे उद्धृत करता है। रूपक की व्याख्या: (1) वृक्ष = शरीर / संसार / कर्मक्षेत्र — दोनों पक्षी एक ही वृक्ष पर। (2) खाने वाला पक्षी = जीवात्मा — सुख-दुःख रूपी कर्मफल खाता है — सदा अगले फल की खोज में। (3) देखने वाला पक्षी = आत्मा / ब्रह्म / साक्षी — शुद्ध चेतना, अचल, अलिप्त, केवल देखता है — पूर्ण शान्ति में। (4) सयुजा = दोनों कभी अलग नहीं — गहनतम अज्ञान में भी ब्रह्म जीव के पास ही — सखा के रूप में। सन्देश: आप दोनों पक्षी हैं — जीवन अनुभव करते हैं (खाने वाला), किन्तु आपका वास्तविक स्वरूप साक्षी (देखने वाला) है। मुक्ति नए वृक्ष पर जाना नहीं — उस पक्षी को देखना है जो आप सदा से हैं।

Eng: The two-birds parable is one of the most ancient, most famous, and most widely quoted images in Indian philosophy: Origin: this mantra first appears in the Ṛg Veda (1.164.20), composed by the seer Dīrghatamas — making it one of the oldest philosophical verses in human history (possibly 1500-1200 BCE). The Muṇḍaka reproduces it nearly verbatim. The Śvetāśvatara (4.6) also quotes it. The mapping: (1) Tree (vṛkṣa) = the body, or the world of saṁsāra, or the field of karma. It is the shared ground of experience — both birds sit on the SAME tree. (2) Eating bird = the jīva (individual self) — engaged with the world, experiencing pleasure and pain, eating the sweet and bitter fruits of karma. This bird is restless — always seeking the next fruit. (3) Watching bird = the ātman/Brahman/witness (sākṣin) — pure awareness, unmoving, uninvolved, simply gazing. This bird is at perfect peace — it has never eaten, never desired, never suffered. (4) Inseparably united (sayujā) = the two are never apart. Even in the deepest ignorance, Brahman is right beside the jīva — on the same tree, as a friend. The message: you are BOTH birds. You experience life (eating bird), but your true nature is the witness (watching bird). Liberation is not going to a new tree — it is seeing the bird you've always been.

dp.q: 🔍 'Abhicākaśīti' — the witness who intensely gazes
dp.a:
अभिचाकशीति क्रिया विशेष ध्यान देने योग्य है — यह साक्षी-आत्मा के स्वरूप को प्रकट करती है। व्याकरण: अभिचाकशीति = √चक्ष् (देखना) का यङ्लुक् (intensive/frequentative) रूप — अर्थात् 'बार-बार, गहनता से, निरन्तर देखना।' साक्षी के बारे में यह क्या प्रकट करता है: (1) साक्षी निष्क्रिय नहीं — गहन ध्यान से देखता है — हर फल, हर सुख-दुःख, पूर्ण स्पष्टता से। (2) साक्षी उदासीन नहीं — intensive रूप गहरी, निरन्तर जागरूकता सूचित करता है। (3) साक्षी कर्ता नहीं — गहनता से देखते हुए भी खाता नहीं — जागरूकता बिना आसक्ति। ध्यान के लिए व्यावहारिक महत्व: 'देखने वाले पक्षी' को खोजने के लिए जागरूकता रोकने की आवश्यकता नहीं — अपने भीतर उस भाग को खोजें जो पहले से देख रहा है — हर विचार, हर भावना के पीछे कुछ है जो बस देखता है — वही दूसरा पक्षी है — वही आप हैं।

Eng: The verb 'abhicākaśīti' deserves special attention — it reveals the nature of the witnessing Self: Grammar: abhicākaśīti is the intensive/frequentative form (yaṅ-luk) of √cakṣ (to see/perceive). The intensive form indicates repeated, intense, or continuous action. So it doesn't mean merely 'sees' but 'gazes intently' or 'watches continuously.' What this reveals about the witness: (1) The witness is not passive — it watches with intense attention. It sees everything — every fruit eaten, every pleasure, every pain — with perfect clarity. (2) The witness is not indifferent — the intensive form suggests deep, sustained awareness, not casual observation. The Self doesn't 'glance' at the world; it gazes. (3) The witness is not acting — despite watching intently, it does NOT eat. It has complete awareness without any involvement. Awareness without attachment. The practical significance for meditation: to find the 'watching bird,' don't try to stop awareness — instead, find the part of you that is already watching. You are already the witness in every moment — behind every thought, behind every emotion, behind every perception, there is something that simply watches. That is the second bird. That is you.

sk: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनीशया शोचति मुह्यमानः जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ||
ro: samāne · vṛkṣe · puruṣaḥ · nimagnaḥ · anīśayā · śocati · muhyamānaḥ · juṣṭaṁ · yadā · paśyati · anyam · īśam · asya · mahimānam · iti · vīta-śokaḥ ||
hi: समान वृक्ष (the same tree) पर पुरुष (the person / जीव) निमग्न (immersed / डूबा हुआ) है — अनीशया (due to helplessness / अशक्ति / lordlessness) शोचति (grieves / शोक करता है), मुह्यमान (deluded / मोहित) होता है। जब (यदा) वह जुष्टम् (the adored / worshipped) अन्यम् ईशम् (the other, the Lord / दूसरे पक्षी — ईश्वर) को पश्यति (sees / देखता है) — और अस्य महिमानम् (His glory) [जानता है] — तब (इति) वीतशोक (free from sorrow / शोक-रहित) हो जाता है।
en: On the same tree (samāne vṛkṣe), the person (puruṣa), immersed (nimagnaḥ), grieves (śocati) due to helplessness (anīśayā), deluded (muhyamānaḥ). But when (yadā) he sees (paśyati) the other (anyam), the Lord (īśam), the adored one (juṣṭam), and [realises] His glory (asya mahimānam) — then he becomes free from sorrow (vīta-śokaḥ).

ws.h: शोक करता है / दुःखी होता है

gr:
व्याकरण: समाने वृक्षे — सप्तमी विभक्ति (locative) — 'उसी वृक्ष पर।' पुरुषः निमग्नः — 'पुरुष' = जीवात्मा; 'निमग्नः' = नि + √मज्ज् (डूबना) — 'डूबा हुआ' — संसार-अनुभव में लीन। अनीशया — अन् + ईश (ईश्वर/प्रभु) + तृतीया — 'ईश्वरत्व-रहित होने से' / 'अशक्ति से' — जीव स्वयं को सीमित, असहाय मानता है। शोचति = √शुच् (शोक करना) — 'दुःखी होता है।' मुह्यमानः = √मुह् (मोहित होना) — शानच् प्रत्यय — 'मोहित होता हुआ।' जुष्टम् = √जुष् (सेवा करना/प्रसन्न होना) — कर्मणि भूतकृदन्त — 'सेवित / आराध्य।' यदा पश्यति = 'जब देखता है' — मोक्ष का क्षण एक 'दर्शन' है — जीव पलटकर दूसरे पक्षी को देखता है। अन्यम् ईशम् = 'दूसरे को, ईश्वर को' — साक्षी जो सदा वहाँ था। वीतशोकः = वीत (गया हुआ) + शोक — 'शोक चला गया' — तत्काल, पूर्ण शोक-मुक्ति।
Eng: From grief to freedom — the emotional heart of the two-birds parable. 'Nimagnaḥ' (ni + √majj) = immersed/drowned. 'Anīśayā' = an-īśa (without lordship/helplessness). Four words paint the jīva's suffering: nimagnaḥ, anīśayā, śocati, muhyamānaḥ. The turning point: 'yadā paśyati' — the moment of recognition. 'Vīta-śokaḥ' = sorrow departs instantly upon seeing the Lord.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'अनीशया' = अज्ञान-वश जीव अपने को अनीश (powerless / limited) मानता है — इसी से शोचति (grieves)। 'अन्यम् ईशम् पश्यति' = जब जीव दूसरे पक्षी (परमात्मा / साक्षी / Brahman) को देखता है — अर्थात् अपनी ब्रह्म-स्वरूपता (Brahman-nature) को पहचानता है — तब 'वीतशोकः' = शोक-मुक्त। 'अन्यम्' = अन्य = वस्तुतः अन्य नहीं — वही अपना आत्मा।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'anīśayā' = due to ignorance, the jīva considers itself powerless/limited — hence it grieves. 'Anyam īśam paśyati' = when the jīva sees the other bird (Paramātmā / witness / Brahman) — i.e., recognises its own Brahman-nature — then 'vīta-śokaḥ' = free from sorrow. 'Anyam' = 'the other' = actually not other but one's own Self.
advaita.ins: You sit on the tree, drowning in experience, eating fruit after fruit, grieving because you feel powerless. Then one day you look up — and see the other bird. The one who's been watching all along. And in that moment you realise: that bird is you. The real you. And sorrow dissolves — because helplessness was only a case of mistaken identity.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'अनीशया' = जीव भगवान् से विच्छिन्न (disconnected) मानता है — इसलिए शोक। 'अन्यम् ईशम् पश्यति' = जब जीव भगवान् (the Lord) — जो सदा उसके साथ (सयुजा, सखाया) हैं — को देखता है, उनका महिमा (glory) जानता है — तब शोक-मुक्त। भगवद्-दर्शन (vision of God) = शोक-निवृत्ति (end of sorrow)।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'anīśayā' = the jīva thinks it is disconnected from God — hence sorrow. 'Anyam īśam paśyati' = when the jīva sees God (the Lord) — who has always been with it (sayujā, sakhāyā) — and knows His glory — then it becomes sorrow-free. Vision of God = end of sorrow.
vishisht.ins: You've been sitting on the tree, feeling alone, overwhelmed, helpless. But look — right next to you sits your oldest friend, the Lord. He's been there through every life, every sorrow, every birth. When you finally turn and see Him — really see Him — sorrow ends. Not because the world changes, but because you see who's been beside you all along.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'निमग्नः' = मनोमय पुरुष (mental being) संसार-अनुभव (world-experience) में डूबा। 'अनीशया' = अहंकार (ego) के कारण — चेतना अपने को सीमित मानती है। 'ईशम् पश्यति' = जब व्यक्ति अन्तरात्मा (psychic being / inner Self) को देखता है — चेतना अपने विश्वव्यापी (universal) स्वरूप को पहचानती है — शोक गिर जाता है।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'nimagnaḥ' = the mental being is drowned in world-experience. 'Anīśayā' = due to the ego — consciousness considers itself limited. 'Īśam paśyati' = when one sees the inner Self (psychic being) — consciousness recognises its universal nature — sorrow falls away.
aurobindo.ins: You're drowning in your own experience — eating every fruit, overwhelmed by every sensation. You feel helpless because the ego tells you you're small, separate, alone. Then you see the other bird — the consciousness that was watching all along, the Self that was never drowning. And the grief that seemed so absolute simply falls away. It was never yours. It was the ego's.

dp.q: 🔍 'Anīśayā' — the root cause of grief
dp.a:
'अनीशया' शब्द जीव के शोक का मूल कारण पहचानता है। व्युत्पत्ति: अन्-ईश = 'ईश्वरत्व-रहित' / 'प्रभुता-रहित' / 'असहायता।' दो व्याख्याएँ: (1) अद्वैत: जीव सोचता है कि 'मैं ईश्वर नहीं हूँ' — अपनी ब्रह्म-स्वरूपता भूल चुका है — शोक भ्रान्त पहचान से — उपाय: साक्षी-पक्षी को पहचानो। (2) विशिष्टाद्वैत: जीव ईश्वर से विच्छिन्न महसूस करता है — शोक अलगाव से — उपाय: पलटकर ईश्वर को देखो जो सदा साथ (सयुजा, सखाया)। दोनों सहमत: शोक का कारण 'न देखना' है — ईश्वर/आत्मा जो सदा उपस्थित, उसे न देखना। उपाय भी 'देखना' — 'यदा पश्यति।' परिणाम तत्काल — 'वीतशोकः।' व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ: शोक बाह्य परिस्थितियों से नहीं — आन्तरिक दृष्टि-दोष से। ईश्वर सदा आपके वृक्ष पर साथ बैठे हैं।

Eng: The word 'anīśayā' identifies the root cause of the jīva's grief: Etymology: an-īśa = 'without lordship' / 'not being the lord' / 'helplessness.' Two readings: (1) Advaita: 'anīśayā' = because the jīva thinks it is NOT the Lord (an-īśa) — i.e., it has forgotten its identity with Brahman. The grief comes from mistaken identity — thinking 'I am a limited, powerless individual' when in fact 'I am Brahman.' The remedy: recognise your identity with the watching bird. (2) Viśiṣṭādvaita: 'anīśayā' = because the jīva is WITHOUT the Lord (an-īśa) — i.e., it has lost its connection with God. The grief comes from separation — feeling alone when God is actually right beside you (sayujā, sakhāyā). The remedy: turn and see the Lord (anyam īśam paśyati). Both readings agree: (a) the root cause of sorrow is a failure of seeing — not seeing the Lord/Self who is always present. (b) The remedy is also a seeing — 'yadā paśyati' (when he sees). (c) The result is immediate — 'vīta-śokaḥ' (sorrow departs). The practical implication: grief is not caused by external circumstances but by an internal failure of vision. The Lord is always right beside you (on the same tree). Your sorrow comes not from the world but from not seeing the companion who shares your tree.

dp.q: 🔍 The moment of recognition — 'yadā paśyati' (when he sees)
dp.a:
'यदा पश्यति' ('जब वह देखता है') — यह मोड़ का क्षण है — शोकग्रस्त जीव पलटकर ईश्वर को देखता है। दर्शन का कारण क्या? मन्त्र 'यदा' (जब) कहता है — कार्य-कारण के बारे में जानबूझकर अस्पष्ट — यह सुझाता है कि पहचान का क्षण पूर्णतः मानवीय प्रयास से उत्पन्न नहीं — इसमें कृपा / स्वतःस्फूर्त मुड़ना है। जीव क्या देखता है? (1) 'अन्यम्' = दूसरा — खाने वाले पक्षी से भिन्न। (2) 'ईशम्' = प्रभु — जिसके पास ऐश्वर्य है। (3) 'जुष्टम्' = आराध्य — स्वभावतः आनन्दमय। (4) 'अस्य महिमानम्' = उसकी महिमा। परिणाम: शोक 'चला जाता है' (वीत) — दबाया नहीं, प्रबन्धित नहीं — विलुप्त। कारण (अनीशया) हटा — प्रभाव विलीन।

Eng: The phrase 'yadā paśyati' ('when he sees') describes the turning point — the moment when the grieving jīva turns and sees the Lord: What triggers the seeing? The mantra uses 'yadā' (when) — a simple temporal conjunction that is deliberately vague about causation. It doesn't say 'after performing rituals,' or 'after studying the Vedas,' or 'after years of meditation.' It says simply 'when.' This vagueness is itself significant — it suggests that the moment of recognition cannot be fully caused or produced by human effort. It involves an element of grace or spontaneous turning. What does the jīva see? (1) 'anyam' = the OTHER — the bird that is different from the eating bird. (2) 'īśam' = the LORD — the one who has mastery, who is sovereign. (3) 'juṣṭam' = the ADORED — the one who is inherently delightful, worshipped by the wise. (4) 'asya mahimānam' = HIS GLORY — the splendour and greatness of the Lord. The result: 'vīta-śokaḥ' = sorrow departs. Not 'sorrow is suppressed' or 'sorrow is managed' — sorrow LEAVES. It goes away entirely. Because the cause of sorrow was 'anīśayā' (not-seeing-the-Lord), and now the Lord is seen. The cause is removed; the effect dissolves. The Kaṭha parallel (1.2.22-23): 'Through the grace of the Creator, he sees the greatness of the Self and becomes free from sorrow.' The Kaṭha explicitly attributes the seeing to grace (dhātu-prasāda) — a dimension that the Muṇḍaka's 'yadā' leaves open.

sk: यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णं कर्तारमीशं पुरुषं ब्रह्मयोनिम् तदा विद्वान्पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैति ||
ro: yadā · paśyaḥ · paśyate · rukma-varṇaṁ · kartāram · īśaṁ · puruṣaṁ · brahma-yonim · tadā · vidvān · puṇya-pāpe · vidhūya · nirañjanaḥ · paramaṁ · sāmyam · upaiti ||
hi: जब (यदा) देखने वाला (पश्यः / the seer) देखता है (पश्यते) रुक्मवर्ण (golden-coloured / सुवर्ण-वर्ण) कर्तारम् (maker / creator / रचयिता), ईशम् (Lord / ईश्वर), पुरुषम् (the Person / पुरुष), ब्रह्मयोनिम् (the source of Brahman / ब्रह्म का कारण) — तब (तदा) विद्वान् (the wise one / ज्ञानी) पुण्य-पापे (merit and sin / पुण्य-पाप दोनों) विधूय (shaking off / झाड़कर), निरञ्जन (stainless / निर्मल / unstained) होकर, परम साम्य (supreme equality / identity / परम समता) को उपैति (attains / प्राप्त करता है)।
en: When (yadā) the seer (paśyaḥ) sees (paśyate) the golden-coloured (rukma-varṇam) maker (kartāram), the Lord (īśam), the Person (puruṣam), the source of Brahman (brahma-yonim) — then (tadā) the wise one (vidvān), shaking off (vidhūya) both merit and sin (puṇya-pāpe), becomes stainless (nirañjanaḥ) and attains (upaiti) supreme equality/identity (paramaṁ sāmyam).
gr:
व्याकरण: यदा पश्यः पश्यते — 'पश्यः' = द्रष्टा (the seer); 'पश्यते' = आत्मनेपद (middle voice) — 'स्वयं के लिए देखता है' — दर्शन आत्म-अनुभव। रुक्मवर्णम् = रुक्म (सुवर्ण/gold) + वर्ण (रंग) — 'स्वर्ण-वर्ण' — स्वयंप्रकाश, अक्षय, शुद्ध। कर्तारम् = √कृ (करना) — 'रचयिता / सृष्टिकर्ता।' ब्रह्मयोनिम् = ब्रह्म (हिरण्यगर्भ/वेद) + योनि (स्रोत/गर्भ) — पुरुष स्वयं ब्रह्म नहीं, ब्रह्म का भी स्रोत — 'कारण का कारण।' पुण्यपापे विधूय — 'पुण्य-पाप' = द्वन्द्व समास — दोनों कर्म (अच्छा और बुरा) 'झाड़ दिए जाते हैं' — मोक्ष दोनों से परे। निरञ्जनः = निर् + अञ्जन (कालिमा/दाग) — 'कलंक-रहित' — आत्मा कभी दागी हुआ ही नहीं — विधूय से जो था वही प्रकट। परमं साम्यम् उपैति — 'साम्यम्' = समता / ऐक्य — अद्वैत में ब्रह्म-ऐक्य, विशिष्टाद्वैत में सारूप्य-सायुज्य।
Eng: The vision of the golden Puruṣa and total liberation. 'Paśyaḥ paśyate' — the seer sees (ātmanepada = self-referential seeing). 'Rukma-varṇam' = golden — self-luminous, imperishable, pure. 'Brahma-yonim' = the source of Brahman/Hiraṇyagarbha — origin of the origin. 'Puṇya-pāpe vidhūya' = shaking off BOTH merit and sin — liberation transcends all karma. 'Nirañjanaḥ' = stainless — the Self was never actually stained. 'Paramaṁ sāmyam' = supreme identity/equality with the Puruṣa.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'रुक्मवर्णम्' = स्वयंप्रकाश ब्रह्म (self-luminous Brahman) — सुवर्ण-वर्ण = शुद्ध चेतना का प्रकाश। 'पुण्यपापे विधूय' = कर्म (karma) — अच्छा (puṇya) और बुरा (pāpa) — दोनों छूटते हैं। 'निरञ्जनः' = आत्मा सदा से शुद्ध — कभी अशुद्ध हुआ ही नहीं। 'परमं साम्यम्' = ब्रह्म-ऐक्य (identity with Brahman) = मोक्ष।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'rukma-varṇam' = self-luminous Brahman — golden colour = the light of pure consciousness. 'Puṇya-pāpe vidhūya' = karma — good and bad — both are shaken off. 'Nirañjanaḥ' = the Self was always pure — it was never impure. 'Paramaṁ sāmyam' = identity with Brahman = mokṣa.
advaita.ins: The golden Puruṣa is not someone else — it's your own Self, shining like gold, never tarnished. When you see it, both good and bad karma fall away like dust. You don't become pure — you discover you were always pure. And you attain supreme identity — not union WITH Brahman, but recognition that you ARE Brahman.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'रुक्मवर्णम्' = भगवान् का दिव्य रूप — सुवर्ण-कान्ति (golden radiance)। 'ब्रह्मयोनिम्' = भगवान् = ब्रह्मा (Hiraṇyagarbha) के भी कारण (source)। 'परमं साम्यम्' = भगवान् के दिव्य गुणों (divine attributes) का समान भोग (equal enjoyment) — ऐक्य (identity) नहीं, सारूप्य-सायुज्य (similarity and union)।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'rukma-varṇam' = the Lord's divine form — golden radiance. 'Brahma-yonim' = the Lord is the source even of Brahmā (Hiraṇyagarbha). 'Paramaṁ sāmyam' = equal enjoyment of the Lord's divine attributes — not identity but similarity and union (sārūpya-sāyujya).
vishisht.ins: See the Lord — golden, radiant, the maker of all, the source of even Brahmā. When you see Him, merit and sin fall away — you don't need them anymore. You become stainless — and you enter into His glory, sharing His divine nature. Not becoming Him — but standing in His light, equal in bliss.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'रुक्मवर्णम्' = अतिमानसिक चेतना (supramental consciousness) — सुवर्ण-वर्ण = सत्य-चेतना (truth-consciousness) का रंग। 'ब्रह्मयोनिम्' = चेतना = सब का मूल-स्रोत। 'परमं साम्यम्' = चेतना-रूपान्तर (consciousness-transformation) — व्यक्तिगत चेतना = विश्व-चेतना = एक।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'rukma-varṇam' = supramental consciousness — golden colour = the colour of truth-consciousness. 'Brahma-yonim' = consciousness is the source of all. 'Paramaṁ sāmyam' = consciousness-transformation — individual consciousness = universal consciousness = one.
aurobindo.ins: The golden Person is truth-consciousness — the supramental light. When you see it, you shake off every stain — not just sin but even merit, because both belong to the mental plane. You become nirañjana — stainless, transparent, pure light. And you attain supreme equality — not with God as separate, but with the truth that is both you and God.

dp.q: 🔍 The golden Puruṣa — why gold?
dp.a:
पुरुष का सुवर्ण-वर्ण (रुक्म-वर्ण) उपनिषदों में बार-बार आता है और गहरा प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ रखता है। सोना क्यों? (1) स्वयंप्रकाशता: सोना अपने स्वभाव से चमकता है — पुरुष स्वयंप्रकाश (self-luminous) — चेतना को किसी बाह्य प्रकाश की आवश्यकता नहीं। (2) अक्षयता: सोना जंग नहीं लगता, क्षय नहीं होता — पुरुष अक्षर (imperishable)। (3) शुद्धता: सोना अन्य तत्त्वों से प्रतिक्रिया नहीं करता — पुरुष निरञ्जन — चेतना कभी अनुभव से अशुद्ध नहीं होती। उपनिषदों में: छान्दोग्य (1.6.6) — 'सूर्य के भीतर हिरण्मय पुरुष'; श्वेताश्वतर (3.8) — 'आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्'; बृहदारण्यक (4.3.11) — 'स्वयं ज्योतिः।' अनुभवात्मक आयाम: गहन ध्यान में साधक प्रायः स्वर्णिम या ज्योतिर्मय प्रकाश देखते हैं — 'सुवर्ण-पुरुष' केवल रूपक नहीं, ध्यान-अनुभव का वर्णन भी हो सकता है।

Eng: The golden colour (rukma-varṇa) of the Puruṣa is a recurring motif in the Upanishads and carries deep symbolic significance: Why gold? (1) Self-luminosity: gold shines by its own nature — it doesn't need an external light source to gleam. Similarly, the Puruṣa is svayam-prakāśa (self-luminous) — consciousness shines by itself, needing no external illumination. (2) Imperishability: gold does not corrode, rust, or decay. It can be buried for millennia and emerge unchanged. Similarly, the Puruṣa is akṣara (imperishable) — consciousness never degrades. (3) Purity: gold is the 'noblest' metal — it doesn't react with other elements, doesn't tarnish, doesn't become impure. Similarly, the Puruṣa is nirañjana (stainless) — consciousness is never polluted by experience. Upanishadic precedents: (1) Chāndogya (1.6.6): 'the Person in the sun is golden' (hiraṇmayaḥ puruṣaḥ). (2) Śvetāśvatara (3.8): 'I know that great Puruṣa, of sun-like lustre, beyond darkness' (āditya-varṇaṁ tamasaḥ parastāt). (3) Bṛhadāraṇyaka (4.3.11): 'In this state, the person is self-luminous' (svayam jyotiḥ). The experiential dimension: meditators across traditions report seeing golden or luminous light in deep meditation — the 'golden Person' may describe an actual meditative experience, not merely a metaphor.

dp.q: 🔍 Shaking off both merit AND sin — beyond good and evil
dp.a:
'पुण्यपापे विधूय' ('पुण्य और पाप दोनों को झाड़कर') — एक क्रान्तिकारी घोषणा। पुण्य (merit) भी क्यों झाड़ा जाता है? मोक्ष के सन्दर्भ में पुण्य भी एक बन्धन है — सोने की ज़ंजीर, पर ज़ंजीर: (1) पुण्य स्वर्गीय भोग देता है — किन्तु अस्थायी — पुण्य क्षीण होने पर पतन (गीता 9.21)। (2) पुण्य आसक्ति पैदा करता है — 'मुझे स्वर्ग चाहिए' — यह कामना संसार-चक्र जारी रखती है। (3) पुण्य अहंकार को पोषित करता है — 'मैं अच्छा व्यक्ति हूँ' — यह अभिमान पृथक् अस्तित्व-भाव को मजबूत करता है। मोक्ष दोनों से परे — मुक्त पुरुष 'निरञ्जन' — शुभ-अशुभ, पुण्य-पाप, स्तुति-निन्दा — सबसे परे।

Eng: The phrase 'puṇya-pāpe vidhūya' ('shaking off both merit and sin') makes a radical claim: Why is merit (puṇya) shaken off? Isn't merit good? In the context of liberation, even merit is a chain — a golden chain, but a chain nonetheless: (1) Puṇya creates heavenly enjoyment: good karma leads to pleasant rebirths, heavenly worlds, divine experiences. But these are temporary — when the merit is exhausted, the soul falls back (kṣīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṁ viśanti — Gītā 9.21). (2) Puṇya creates attachment: the desire for merit creates attachment to results — 'I want to go to heaven,' 'I want a good rebirth.' This desire itself perpetuates saṁsāra. (3) Puṇya reinforces the ego: 'I am a good person,' 'I have done great deeds' — this pride strengthens the sense of separate selfhood, which is the root of bondage. Liberation is beyond BOTH: the Muṇḍaka's teaching is unambiguous — liberation requires shaking off ALL karma, positive and negative. The liberated one is 'nirañjana' (stainless) — beyond good and evil, beyond merit and sin, beyond praise and blame. The Kaṭha parallel (1.2.14): 'The Self is beyond what is done and what is not done, beyond what has happened and what is to happen.' The Gītā's echo (2.50): 'Yoga is skill in action' (yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam) — acting without attachment to results, whether good or bad.

sk: प्राणो ह्येष यः सर्वभूतैर्विभाति विजानन्विद्वान्भवते नातिवादी आत्मक्रीड आत्मरतिः क्रियावानेष ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः ||
ro: prāṇaḥ · hi · eṣaḥ · yaḥ · sarva-bhūtaiḥ · vibhāti · vijānan · vidvān · bhavate · na · ativādī · ātma-krīḍaḥ · ātma-ratiḥ · kriyāvān · eṣaḥ · brahma-vidāṁ · variṣṭhaḥ ||
hi: वह (एषः) प्राण (life / consciousness) ही है — जो सर्वभूतैः (all beings) से विभाति (shines / प्रकाशित होता है)। [इसे] विजानन् (understanding) विद्वान् (the wise one / ज्ञानी) भवते (becomes) — अतिवादी (a boaster / excessive talker) नहीं (न)। [वह] आत्मक्रीड (one who sports in the Self / आत्मा में खेलने वाला), आत्मरति (one who delights in the Self / आत्मा में रमण करने वाला), क्रियावान् (active / कर्मशील) — वह (एषः) ब्रह्मविदाम् वरिष्ठः (the best among knowers of Brahman / ब्रह्मज्ञानियों में श्रेष्ठ) है।
en: He is indeed prāṇa (life/consciousness) (prāṇo hy eṣaḥ), who shines (vibhāti) through all beings (sarva-bhūtaiḥ). Understanding this (vijānan), the wise one (vidvān) does not talk excessively (na ativādī). [Rather, he is] one who sports in the Self (ātma-krīḍa), delights in the Self (ātma-rati), [and is] active (kriyāvān). He is the best (variṣṭha) among the knowers of Brahman (brahma-vidām).

ws.h: सब प्राणियों से / सब जीवों से
अत्यधिक बोलने वाला / डींगें मारने वाला

ws.e: one who sports in the Self

ws.h: आत्मा में रमण करने वाला / आत्मानन्दी
ws.e: one who delights in the Self

gr:
व्याकरण: प्राणः हि एषः — 'प्राणः' = जीवन-शक्ति / चेतना; 'हि' = निश्चय ही; 'एषः' = वह (पुरुष/ब्रह्म)। सर्वभूतैः विभाति — 'सर्वभूतैः' = तृतीया बहुवचन — 'सब प्राणियों के माध्यम से'; 'विभाति' = वि + √भा (चमकना) — 'विशेष रूप से प्रकाशित होता है।' विजानन् = वि + √ज्ञा — शतृ प्रत्यय — 'विशेष रूप से जानते हुए / गहरी समझ से।' न अतिवादी — 'अतिवादी' = अति + √वद् (बोलना) — 'अत्यधिक बोलने वाला / डींगें हाँकने वाला' — सच्चा ज्ञानी वाचाल नहीं, मौन ज्ञान का लक्षण। आत्मक्रीडः = आत्मन् + √क्रीड् (खेलना) — 'आत्मा में विहार करने वाला।' आत्मरतिः = आत्मन् + √रम् (रमना) — 'आत्मा में आनन्दित।' क्रियावान् = क्रिया + वत् (मतुप् प्रत्यय) — 'कर्मशील / सक्रिय' — यह अत्यन्त महत्वपूर्ण है: ब्रह्मज्ञानी निष्क्रिय या संन्यासी नहीं — सक्रिय है — गीता के कर्मयोग की पूर्वध्वनि। ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः = ब्रह्मज्ञानियों में श्रेष्ठतम।
Eng: Portrait of the Brahman-knower. Five key traits: (1) na ativādī — doesn't boast; (2) ātma-krīḍa — plays in the Self; (3) ātma-rati — delights in the Self; (4) kriyāvān — active/engaged; (5) brahma-vidāṁ variṣṭha — the best among knowers. 'Kriyāvān' refutes the idea that the knower is passive — true knowledge leads to a different KIND of activity, born from fullness, not lack.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'आत्मक्रीडः आत्मरतिः' = ज्ञानी का आनन्द आत्मा में — बाह्य विषयों (external objects) में नहीं। 'न अतिवादी' = ज्ञानी वाचाल (verbose) नहीं — मौन (silence) ज्ञान का लक्षण। 'क्रियावान्' = शंकर कहते हैं यह 'क्रिया' = आत्म-ज्ञान की 'क्रिया' — लौकिक कर्म नहीं (किन्तु अन्य टीकाकार कर्म-योग मानते हैं)।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'ātma-krīḍa ātma-rati' = the wise one's bliss is in the Self — not in external objects. 'Na ativādī' = the wise one is not verbose — silence is the mark of knowledge. 'Kriyāvān' = Shankara says this 'kriyā' = the 'activity' of Self-knowledge — not worldly action (but other commentators take it as karma-yoga).
advaita.ins: The greatest knower of Brahman doesn't lecture you about Brahman — they radiate it. They play in their own Self, delight in their own Being, and remain active — not from desire but from overflowing joy. They don't talk excessively. They live it. That's the highest.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'आत्मक्रीडः' = भगवान् में क्रीड़ा (playing in God) — भक्ति-आनन्द। 'क्रियावान्' = भक्त कर्मशील (active) रहता है — भगवान् की सेवा में। 'ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठः' = भक्तों में श्रेष्ठ — जो भगवद्-ज्ञान और भगवद्-सेवा दोनों करता है।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'ātma-krīḍa' = playing in God — the bliss of devotion. 'Kriyāvān' = the devotee remains active — in the service of God. 'Brahma-vidāṁ variṣṭha' = the best among devotees — one who both knows God and serves God.
vishisht.ins: The greatest knower of God plays in divine joy, delights in God's presence, and remains active — serving, working, offering. They don't sit around boasting about their knowledge. They live it — joyfully, humbly, actively. That's what makes them the best.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'आत्मक्रीडः' = चेतना अपने में आनन्दित (consciousness delighting in itself)। 'क्रियावान्' = ज्ञानी निष्क्रिय (inactive) नहीं — सक्रिय (active) — चेतना की गतिशीलता (dynamism of consciousness) = कर्म-योग। ज्ञान = निवृत्ति (withdrawal) नहीं — चेतना का पूर्ण प्रकटीकरण (full manifestation)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'ātma-krīḍa' = consciousness delighting in itself. 'Kriyāvān' = the knower is NOT inactive — they are active — the dynamism of consciousness = karma-yoga. Knowledge ≠ withdrawal — it is the full manifestation of consciousness.
aurobindo.ins: The knower doesn't retreat from life — they dive deeper in. They play in the Self, delight in being, and remain fully active. Because knowledge isn't withdrawal — it's fuller engagement. When consciousness knows itself, it doesn't stop — it flows more freely, acts more purely, creates more joyfully.

dp.q: 🔍 'Kriyāvān' — the active knower, not the passive sage
dp.a:
'क्रियावान्' (कर्मशील / सक्रिय) इस मन्त्र के सबसे महत्वपूर्ण शब्दों में से एक है। क्यों महत्वपूर्ण: ब्रह्मज्ञानी की सामान्य छवि एक निवृत्त, निष्क्रिय, संसार-त्यागी तपस्वी की है — यह मन्त्र उस छवि का सीधा खण्डन करता है — ब्रह्मज्ञानियों में श्रेष्ठ क्रियावान् (सक्रिय) है। कौन-सा कर्म? अन्तर कर्म के स्रोत में है: (1) सामान्य कर्म = काम, भय, वासना से प्रेरित — बाँधता है; (2) ज्ञानी का कर्म = आत्म-आनन्द (ātma-krīḍa, ātma-rati) से — परिपूर्णता से उत्पन्न, अभाव से नहीं। गीता का विस्तार (3.17-18, 3.20): 'जो आत्मा में ही रत है... उसका कोई कर्तव्य नहीं' — फिर भी जनक आदि ने कर्म से ही सिद्धि प्राप्त की। विरोधाभास: मुक्त व्यक्ति को कर्म से कुछ पाना नहीं, फिर भी करता है — परिपूर्णता से, अभाव से नहीं।

Eng: The word 'kriyāvān' (active / engaged in action) is one of the most significant words in this mantra: Why it matters: the common stereotype of the Brahman-knower is a withdrawn, passive, world-renouncing ascetic. This mantra directly contradicts that image — the best among knowers of Brahman is kriyāvān (active). What kind of action? The key difference is the source of action: (1) Ordinary action: driven by desire (kāma), fear (bhaya), or habit (vāsanā). This action binds — it creates karma and perpetuates saṁsāra. (2) The knower's action: driven by Self-delight (ātma-krīḍa, ātma-rati). The knower acts because action is a natural expression of the overflowing joy of the Self — not because they want something. The Gītā's elaboration (3.17-18): 'For one who delights in the Self alone, who is satisfied with the Self, who is content in the Self — for such a one there is nothing to be done. Such a person has no purpose in what is done or what is not done.' Yet Kṛṣṇa also says (3.20): 'Janaka and others attained perfection through action alone.' The paradox: the liberated person has nothing to gain from action, yet acts — from fullness, not lack. The Chāndogya parallel (7.25.2): describes the Self-knower as 'svarāṭ' (self-sovereign) — autonomous, acting freely, not compelled by anything external.

dp.q: 🔍 'Na ativādī' — the silence of the knower
dp.a:
'न अतिवादी' ('अत्यधिक न बोलने वाला / डींगें न हाँकने वाला') — सच्चे ब्रह्मज्ञानी का एक महत्वपूर्ण गुण। मौन क्यों? (1) ब्रह्म वाणी से परे — तैत्तिरीय (2.9.1): 'यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते' — 'जहाँ से वाणी लौट आती है' — जिसने शब्दातीत देखा, स्वभावतः मौन। (2) ज्ञान विनम्रता लाता है — ज्ञान से पूर्व शब्दों पर विश्वास, ज्ञान के बाद शब्दों की अपर्याप्तता का बोध। (3) ज्ञानी को कुछ सिद्ध नहीं करना — 'अतिवादी' में 'डींग हाँकना' का अर्थ भी — ज्ञानी को मान्यता की आवश्यकता नहीं। व्यावहारिक परीक्षा: क्या व्यक्ति अपने ज्ञान के बारे में अत्यधिक बोलता है? यदि हाँ — सम्भवतः 'ब्रह्मविदां वरिष्ठ' नहीं। ध्यान दें — 'न अतिवादी' कहा, 'न वादी' (बिल्कुल न बोलने वाला) नहीं — ज्ञानी बोल सकता है — किन्तु मर्यादित, सार्थक, परिपूर्णता से।

Eng: The phrase 'na ativādī' ('not an excessive talker / not a boaster') reveals an important quality of the true Brahman-knower: Why silence? (1) Brahman is beyond words: the Taittirīya (2.9.1) says: 'yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha' — 'from which words return, unable to reach it, along with the mind.' One who has seen what is beyond words naturally falls silent about it. (2) Knowledge brings humility: before realisation, one may talk confidently about Brahman from books and logic. After realisation, one realises how inadequate words are — and speaks less. (3) The knower has nothing to prove: 'ativādī' carries the connotation of 'boasting' — talking to impress, to establish superiority, to win arguments. The Brahman-knower has transcended the need for validation; they have found their identity in the Self, not in others' opinions. The practical test: the Muṇḍaka offers a simple diagnostic for genuine spiritual attainment — does the person talk excessively about their knowledge? If yes, they are probably not a 'brahma-vidāṁ variṣṭha' (the best among knowers). The best among knowers plays in the Self, delights in the Self, remains active — and does NOT boast. Not silence vs. speech: the instruction is 'na ativādī' — not 'na vādī' (not a speaker at all). The knower CAN speak — but doesn't speak excessively. Their speech is measured, purposeful, and comes from a place of fullness, not a need to fill silence.

sk: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म ततोऽन्नमभिजायते अन्नात्प्राणो मनः सत्यं लोकाः कर्मसु चामृतम् ||
ro: tapasā · cīyate · brahma · tataḥ · annam · abhijāyate · annāt · prāṇaḥ · manaḥ · satyaṁ · lokāḥ · karmasu · ca · amṛtam ||
hi: तपसा (by tapas / तप से) ब्रह्म (Brahman) चीयते (is built up / संचित होता है)। ततः (from that) अन्नम् (food / matter) अभिजायते (is born)। अन्न से प्राण (life-breath), मनः (mind), सत्यम् (truth), लोकाः (worlds), और कर्मसु अमृतम् (in actions, immortality) [उत्पन्न होते हैं]।
en: By tapas (austerity), Brahman is built up (cīyate); from that, food/matter (anna) is born. From food [come] prāṇa, manas (mind), truth (satya), the worlds (lokāḥ), and immortality in actions (karmasu amṛtam).

ws.h: संचित होता है / निर्मित होता है
उत्पन्न होता है / जन्म लेता है

gr:
व्याकरण: तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म — 'तपसा' = तृतीया एकवचन (instrumental) — 'तप के द्वारा'; 'चीयते' = √चि (संचित करना) — कर्मणि (passive) — 'संचित किया जाता है / निर्मित होता है।' ततः अन्नम् अभिजायते — 'ततः' = उससे; 'अभिजायते' = अभि + √जन् — 'प्रकट होता है / उत्पन्न होता है।' अन्नात् प्राणः मनः सत्यं लोकाः — अन्न से क्रमशः सृष्टि: प्राण → मन → सत्य → लोक। कर्मसु च अमृतम् — 'कर्मों में अमरत्व' — कर्म में भी अमृत-तत्त्व। 2.2.10 से पुनरुक्ति — संरचनात्मक सेतु (structural bridge) — मुण्डक 2 (ध्यान-शिक्षा) को मुण्डक 3 (मोक्ष-शिक्षा) से जोड़ता है। तृतीय मुण्डक में 'तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म' का व्यक्तिगत अर्थ भी — साधक अपने तप से ब्रह्म-ज्ञान 'संचित' करता है।
Eng: Repetition from 2.2.10 serving as structural bridge. 'Tapasā' (instrumental of tapas). 'Cīyate' (passive of √ci — 'to accumulate'). In Muṇḍaka 3 context, takes personal meaning — the aspirant builds up Brahman-knowledge through their own tapas. The creation hierarchy: tapas → anna → prāṇa → manas → satya → lokāḥ → amṛta.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — पुनरुक्ति (repetition) = बल-प्रदान (emphasis)। 'तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म' = साधक (aspirant) का तप = ज्ञान-साधन (means of knowledge)। तप से ब्रह्म-ज्ञान 'संचित' (accumulated) होता है — क्रमशः (gradually) — अन्ततः मोक्ष।
advaita.en: Shankara says repetition = emphasis. 'Tapasā cīyate brahma' = the aspirant's tapas = the means of knowledge. Through tapas, Brahman-knowledge is 'accumulated' — gradually — ultimately leading to mokṣa.
advaita.ins: The verse repeats — and repetition is emphasis. Build up Brahman-knowledge through tapas, brick by brick. From that knowledge, everything flows — life, mind, truth, worlds, immortality in action. The same process that created the universe is the process by which you realise it.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — पुनरुक्ति = दृढ़ीकरण (reinforcement)। भक्ति-तप (devotional tapas) से भगवद्-ज्ञान (God-knowledge) वृद्धि (grows) होती है — और उस ज्ञान से सब कुछ — प्राण, मन, सत्य, लोक — सार्थक (meaningful) हो जाता है।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says repetition = reinforcement. Through devotional tapas, God-knowledge grows — and from that knowledge, everything — prāṇa, mind, truth, worlds — becomes meaningful.
vishisht.ins: The Upanishad says it twice — so listen twice. Devotion builds up knowledge of God. And when you know God, everything becomes meaningful — your breath, your mind, your work, your world. Even your everyday actions carry the spark of the immortal.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — पुनरुक्ति = संरचनात्मक सेतु (structural bridge)। चेतना-शक्ति (tapas) = सृष्टि (creation) का कारण (Muṇḍaka 2) और मोक्ष (liberation) का कारण (Muṇḍaka 3) — एक ही शक्ति।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says repetition = structural bridge. Consciousness-force (tapas) = the cause of creation (Muṇḍaka 2) AND the cause of liberation (Muṇḍaka 3) — the same force.
aurobindo.ins: The same tapas that created the universe is the tapas that liberates you. Build up consciousness through practice. From consciousness, everything emerges — life, mind, truth, worlds, immortality. The creative force and the liberating force are one.

dp.q: 🔍 Why this mantra repeats from 2.2.10
dp.a:
यह मन्त्र मुण्डक 2.2.10 की शब्दशः पुनरुक्ति है। यह त्रुटि या प्रक्षेपण नहीं — पुनरुक्ति के महत्वपूर्ण संरचनात्मक और शैक्षणिक कार्य हैं: (1) संरचनात्मक सेतु: द्वितीय मुण्डक (ध्यान-मार्ग) को तृतीय मुण्डक (मोक्ष-शिक्षा) से जोड़ता है — वही तप जो ध्यान-खण्ड में सिखाया गया, मोक्ष-खण्ड का आधार है। (2) बल-प्रदान: मौखिक परम्परा में पुनरुक्ति = बल — गुरु जब यह मन्त्र पुनः कहता है, शिष्य पहचानता है — यह महत्वपूर्ण है। (3) दोहरा अनुप्रयोग: 2.2.10 में 'तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म' = ब्रह्म का सृष्टि-तप; 3.1.5 में = साधक का अपना तप — सृष्टि-तप और मोक्ष-तप एक ही शक्ति। (4) स्मृति-आधार: मौखिक संचारण में दोहराए गए मन्त्र 'स्मृति-अंकुश' — शिष्य इनसे आसपास की शिक्षा स्मरण कर सकता है।

Eng: This mantra is a verbatim repetition of Muṇḍaka 2.2.10. Far from being an error or an interpolation, the repetition serves important structural and pedagogical functions: (1) Structural bridge: the verse links the second Muṇḍaka (the meditation path) to the third Muṇḍaka (the liberation teachings). By placing it at the junction, the Muṇḍaka says: the same tapas that was taught in the meditation section is the foundation of the liberation section. (2) Emphasis: in an oral tradition, repetition IS emphasis. When the teacher says this mantra again, the student recognises it and understands: this is important — remember it. (3) Dual application: in 2.2.10, 'tapasā cīyate brahma' referred primarily to Brahman's creative tapas — the universe is created through Brahman's knowledge-tapas. In 3.1.5, the same phrase takes on a personal meaning — the aspirant 'builds up' Brahman-knowledge through their own tapas (discipline, meditation, study). The creation-tapas and the liberation-tapas are the same energy, applied at different scales. (4) Mnemonic anchor: in the oral transmission of the Upanishads, repeated verses served as 'hooks' for memory — the student could use them to recall the surrounding teachings.

dp.q: 🔍 The aspirant's tapas — building up Brahman within
dp.a:
तृतीय मुण्डक के सन्दर्भ में 'तपसा चीयते ब्रह्म' का गहरा व्यक्तिगत अर्थ — साधक अपने भीतर ब्रह्म-ज्ञान संचित करता है। साधक का तप क्या है? (1) श्रवण: गुरु-उपदेश सुनना। (2) मनन: सुने हुए पर गहन चिन्तन — सन्देह निवारण। (3) निदिध्यासन: आत्मा पर सतत ध्यान — धनुष-बाण ध्यान, ओंकार-ध्यान, हृदय-केन्द्र ध्यान। (4) नैतिक अनुशासन: सत्य, अहिंसा, ब्रह्मचर्य। 'चीयते' (संचित होता है) क्यों? अनुभूति सामान्यतः तत्काल नहीं — समय के साथ 'संचित' होती है, जैसे अग्नि-वेदी ईंट-ईंट बनती है — हर ध्यान-सत्र, हर नैतिक निर्णय एक ईंट — अन्ततः अनुभूति की अग्नि प्रज्वलित। फल: साधक के तप से सृष्टि का पूरा क्रम ब्रह्म-अभिव्यक्ति के रूप में प्रकट होता है।

Eng: In the context of the third Muṇḍaka, 'tapasā cīyate brahma' takes on a deeply personal meaning — the aspirant builds up Brahman-realisation within themselves: What is the aspirant's tapas? (1) Śravaṇa (hearing): listening to the teacher's instruction — absorbing the Upanishadic teaching. (2) Manana (reflection): thinking deeply about what has been heard — resolving doubts, understanding implications. (3) Nididhyāsana (deep meditation): sustained contemplation on the Self — the bow-and-arrow meditation, OM-meditation, heart-centre meditation. (4) Ethical discipline: truthfulness (satya), non-violence (ahiṁsā), self-restraint (brahmacarya) — the moral foundation without which knowledge cannot ripen. Why 'cīyate' (built up)? Realisation is not typically instantaneous — it is 'accumulated' over time, like building a fire-altar brick by brick. Each meditation session, each ethical choice, each moment of self-awareness is a 'brick' in the altar of Brahman-knowledge. Over time, the altar rises — and the fire of realisation blazes upon it. The result: 'from that, anna (food/matter) is born' — from the aspirant's tapas, the entire hierarchy of existence reveals itself as Brahman's expression. Prāṇa, mind, truth, worlds, and even immortality in action — all are seen as flowing from the one Brahman that the aspirant has 'built up' through practice.

sk: यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित्सर्वलक्ष्मीमयो हि सः तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्म नाम रूपं अन्नं च जायते तदेतत्सत्यम् ||
ro: yaḥ · sarva-jñaḥ · sarva-vit · sarva-lakṣmī-mayaḥ · hi · saḥ · tasmāt · etat · brahma · nāma · rūpaṁ · annaṁ · ca · jāyate · tat · etat · satyam ||
hi: जो सर्वज्ञ (omniscient) है, सर्ववित् (all-knowing) है, सर्वलक्ष्मीमय (endowed with all glory) ही वह है — उससे यह ब्रह्म (Vedic reality), नाम (name), रूप (form), और अन्न (food/matter) जायते (is born)। वह यह सत्यम् (truth) है।
en: He who is omniscient (sarva-jña), all-knowing (sarva-vit), endowed with all glory (sarva-lakṣmī-maya) — He indeed is that. From Him are born this Brahman, name (nāma), form (rūpa), and food (anna). This is the truth (tat etat satyam).

ws.h: सब ऐश्वर्य से युक्त / समस्त वैभवमय

gr:
व्याकरण: सर्वज्ञः = सर्व + √ज्ञा — 'सब जानने वाला' — सामान्य ज्ञान। सर्ववित् = सर्व + √विद् — 'विशेष ज्ञान' / 'प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव से जानने वाला' — शंकर दो भेद करते हैं: सर्वज्ञ = सामान्य ज्ञान, सर्ववित् = विशेष/प्रत्यक्ष ज्ञान। सर्वलक्ष्मीमयः = सर्व + लक्ष्मी (ऐश्वर्य/श्री) + मय (से पूर्ण) — 'समस्त वैभव से परिपूर्ण।' तस्मात् ... जायते — 'उससे ... उत्पन्न होता है' — सृष्टि-क्रम: ब्रह्म, नाम, रूप, अन्न। तदेतत्सत्यम् = तत् + एतत् + सत्यम् — 'वह यही सत्य है' — अन्तिम प्रमाणीकरण। 2.2.11 से पुनरुक्ति — 3.1.5 के साथ मिलकर 'दोहरा सेतु' — द्वितीय मुण्डक का समापन-युग्म तृतीय मुण्डक के मध्य-भाग का उद्घाटन बनता है।
Eng: Repetition from 2.2.11. 'Sarva-jña' (√jñā = general knowing) vs 'sarva-vit' (√vid = direct/particular knowing) — Shankara distinguishes the two. 'Sarva-lakṣmī-maya' = filled with all glory. 'Tat etat satyam' = the concluding seal of truth. Creates a 'double bridge' with 3.1.5, carrying over the complete teaching from Muṇḍaka 2.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — पुनरुक्ति (repetition) = विषय की पुष्टि (confirmation of the topic) और नये प्रकरण (section) का आरम्भ। वही सर्वज्ञ, सर्ववित्, सर्वलक्ष्मीमय ब्रह्म — जिसका ध्यान (meditation) बताया गया — अब उसकी प्राप्ति (attainment) बताई जाएगी।
advaita.en: Shankara says repetition = confirmation of the topic and beginning of a new section. The same omniscient, all-knowing, all-glorious Brahman — whose meditation was taught — now its attainment will be described.
advaita.ins: The truth repeats because it's unchanging. The same Brahman you meditated on in the last section is the Brahman you'll attain in this one. All-knowing, all-glorious — the source of names, forms, and matter. This is the truth. Now — how to realise it.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — वही सर्वगुण-सम्पन्न (all-qualified) भगवान् — जिनका ज्ञान (knowledge) और भक्ति (devotion) बताई गई — अब उनकी प्राप्ति (attainment) का वर्णन। 'सत्यम्' = भगवान् = परम सत्य — सर्वदा, सर्वत्र।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says the same all-qualified Lord — whose knowledge and devotion were taught — now His attainment will be described. 'Satyam' = the Lord = the supreme truth — always, everywhere.
vishisht.ins: The same all-glorious Lord you've been learning about — omniscient, all-beautiful, the source of everything — now the Upanishad will teach how to reach Him. The truth doesn't change between sections. It's the same truth, the same Lord, the same goal.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — पुनरुक्ति = चेतना की एकता (unity of consciousness) की पुष्टि। सृष्टि (creation) और मोक्ष (liberation) = एक ही चेतना के दो मुख (two faces of one consciousness)। सत्यम् = यही अन्तिम सत्य।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says repetition = confirmation of the unity of consciousness. Creation and liberation = two faces of one consciousness. Satyam = this is the final truth.
aurobindo.ins: Creation and liberation are two faces of the same truth. The consciousness that creates the universe is the consciousness that liberates you. All-knowing, all-glorious — it's the same light, whether you see it as the origin of the world or the destination of the soul.

dp.q: 🔍 The double repetition (3.1.5-6 = 2.2.10-11) as structural device
dp.a:
दोहरी पुनरुक्ति (3.1.5-6 = 2.2.10-11) एक सोची-समझी संरचनात्मक युक्ति है। क्या बनती है: द्वितीय मुण्डक (ध्यान-शिक्षा) और तृतीय मुण्डक (मोक्ष-शिक्षा) के बीच 'सेतु' — एक ही मन्त्र-युग्म एक खण्ड बन्द करता है और अगला खोलता है। सन्देश: ध्यान और मोक्ष में कोई अन्तराल नहीं — वही ब्रह्म जो ध्यान का विषय (मुण्डक 2), वही मोक्ष का ब्रह्म (मुण्डक 3)। वही तप जो सृष्टि करता है, वही ज्ञान संचित करता है। मौखिक परम्परा: ऐसी पुनरुक्तियाँ 'खण्ड-चिह्न' (section markers) का काम करतीं — पाठकर्ता और श्रोता को बताती हैं कि एक शिक्षा-इकाई समाप्त और दूसरी आरम्भ।

Eng: The double repetition — mantras 3.1.5 and 3.1.6 reproducing 2.2.10 and 2.2.11 verbatim — is a deliberate structural device: What it creates: a 'bridge' or 'hinge' between the second Muṇḍaka (meditation teaching) and the third Muṇḍaka (liberation teaching). The same pair of verses closes one section and opens the next, creating seamless continuity. The message: there is no gap between meditation and liberation, between practice and attainment. The same Brahman that is the object of meditation (Muṇḍaka 2) is the Brahman that is attained through liberation (Muṇḍaka 3). The same tapas that creates the universe is the tapas that builds up knowledge. Oral tradition context: in the oral transmission of the Upanishads, such repetitions served as 'section markers' — they told the reciter (and the listener) that one teaching-unit was ending and another beginning. They also served as memory anchors — the student could use the familiar verses to recall the surrounding material. The pattern in the Muṇḍaka: the Muṇḍaka uses several such framing devices: (1) 'somya' (O gentle one) at the start and end of 2.1 (mantras 1 and 10). (2) 'tat etat satyam' (this is the truth) at 2.2.11 and 3.1.6. (3) The two-birds parable at 3.1.1-2 echoing ṚV 1.164.20. These devices create a tightly structured text despite its oral origins.

dp.q: 🔍 The continuity from meditation to liberation
dp.a:
दोहरी पुनरुक्ति एक मुख्य दार्शनिक बिन्दु की ओर संकेत करती है: ध्यान और मोक्ष सतत हैं, पृथक् नहीं। प्रवाह: मुण्डक 2 ने सिखाया कैसे ध्यान करें — धनुष-बाण, ॐ, हृदय-केन्द्र। मुण्डक 3 सिखाता है ध्यान सफल होने पर क्या होता है — दो पक्षी, सुवर्ण-पुरुष, हृदय-ग्रन्थि का छेदन, 'ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मैव भवति।' सेतु-मन्त्र कहते हैं: ध्यान में जो तप, ब्रह्म, सत्य था — वही मोक्ष में। साधना से फल तक कोई 'छलांग' नहीं — केवल गहनता। तप 'संचित' होता जाता है — एक सीमा पर हृदय-ग्रन्थि टूटती है, सुवर्ण-पुरुष दिखता है, शोक विलीन। व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ: साधना से बिल्कुल असम्बद्ध किसी नाटकीय 'ज्ञान-क्षण' की प्रतीक्षा न करें — मोक्ष ध्यान से उगता है, जैसे फूल से फल।

Eng: The double repetition signals a key philosophical point: meditation and liberation are continuous, not separate: The flow: Muṇḍaka 2 taught HOW to meditate — the bow-and-arrow, OM, the heart-centre. Muṇḍaka 3 teaches WHAT HAPPENS when meditation succeeds — the two birds, the vision of the golden Puruṣa, the cutting of the heart-knot, the declaration 'brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati.' The bridge verses (3.1.5-6) say: the same tapas, the same Brahman, the same truth that was the subject of meditation IS the subject of liberation. There is no 'leap' from practice to result — only deepening. The tapas that 'builds up' Brahman in meditation eventually reaches a critical mass — and the heart-knot snaps, and the golden Puruṣa is seen, and sorrow departs. The practical implication: don't wait for a dramatic 'moment of enlightenment' that is totally discontinuous with your practice. Liberation grows organically from meditation, as a fruit grows from a flower. Keep building the fire-altar, brick by brick. The fire will blaze when the altar is ready.

sk: तदेतत्सत्यं कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा सन्ततानि तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके ||
ro: tat · etat · satyam · mantreṣu · karmāṇi · kavayaḥ · yāni · apaśyan · tāni · tretāyāṁ · bahudhā · santatāni · tāni · ācaratha · niyataṁ · satya-kāmāḥ · eṣaḥ · vaḥ · panthāḥ · su-kṛtasya · loke ||
hi: वह यह सत्य है। मन्त्रों में कवियों (seers) ने जो कर्माणि (ritual actions) देखे — वे त्रेतायाम् (three fires) में बहुधा सन्ततानि (spread out) हैं। हे सत्यकामाः (lovers of truth)! उन्हें नियमपूर्वक आचरण करो। यह तुम्हारा मार्ग है — सुकृत (good deeds) के लोक में।
en: This is the truth. The ritual actions that the seers saw in the mantras — those are spread in many ways in the three fires. Practise them regularly, O lovers of truth! This is your path in the world of good deeds.

ws.h: अनेक प्रकार से / बहुत तरह से

gr:
व्याकरण: तदेतत्सत्यम् — 'वह यही सत्य है' — प्रमाणीकरण-सूत्र। कर्माणि कवयः यानि अपश्यन् — 'कवयः' = ऋषि/द्रष्टा — वे जिन्होंने मन्त्रों को 'देखा' (अपश्यन् = √दृश् का लुङ्/अनद्यतन — 'प्राचीन काल में देखा')। त्रेतायाम् = त्रि + इता — 'तीन अग्नियों' (गार्हपत्य, दक्षिणाग्नि, आहवनीय) में। बहुधा सन्ततानि = 'अनेक प्रकार से विस्तृत' — विविध यज्ञ-कर्म। तानि आचरथ नियतम् — 'आचरथ' = आ + √चर् (आचरण करना) — लोट् (imperative) बहुवचन — 'तुम सब आचरण करो'; 'नियतम्' = नियमपूर्वक। सत्यकामाः = सत्य + काम (इच्छा) — 'सत्य चाहने वाले' — सम्बोधन — पात्रता-सूचक। सुकृतस्य लोके = पुण्य-लोक में — कर्म-फल = स्वर्गादि, मोक्ष नहीं। 2.2.8 से पुनरुक्ति — तीन पुनरावृत्त मन्त्रों (3.1.5-7) में तीसरा — ज्ञान-शिक्षा और कर्म-शिक्षा दोनों को वहन करता पूर्ण सेतु।
Eng: Repetition from 2.2.8. 'Kavayaḥ apaśyan' — the seers 'saw' (not composed) the rituals. 'Tretāyām' = in the three sacrificial fires. 'Ācaratha niyatam' = imperative plural — 'practise regularly.' 'Satya-kāmāḥ' = lovers of truth — the qualification. 'Sukṛtasya loke' = in the world of merit — karma-fruit, not mokṣa. Third of the triple bridge (3.1.5-7 = 2.2.10, 2.2.11, 2.2.8).

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — पुनरुक्ति = चित्त-शुद्धि (purification of mind) के लिए कर्म-मार्ग (karma path) की पुनःपुष्टि। कर्म = ज्ञान का पूर्वाङ्ग (preparatory limb) — ज्ञान का विकल्प (substitute) नहीं। 'सुकृतस्य लोके' = कर्म-फल = पुण्यलोक, मोक्ष नहीं।
advaita.en: Shankara says repetition = reconfirmation of the karma-path for mental purification. Karma = the preparatory limb of knowledge — not a substitute. 'Sukṛtasya loke' = karma-fruit = meritorious world, not mokṣa.
advaita.ins: The ritual path appears again — because it's still valid, still needed, still a real path. But notice where it leads: the world of good deeds. Beautiful, but not final. The final teaching comes next — the heart-knot and the river reaching the ocean.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — कर्म + भक्ति + ज्ञान = समन्वित मार्ग (integrated path)। ऋषियों ने 'देखे' = दिव्य-दृष्टि (divine vision) से। कर्म भगवान् की आराधना (worship of God) के रूप में = मोक्ष-मार्ग का अंग।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says karma + bhakti + jñāna = integrated path. Seers 'saw' them through divine vision. Karma performed as worship of God = a component of the liberation-path.
vishisht.ins: The seers saw these rituals in vision — they're real, divinely ordained. Practise them with truth as your desire, as offerings to God. This is your starting path. The full path integrates action, devotion, and knowledge — all flowing toward God.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — ऋषि-दृष्ट कर्म = चेतना के बाह्य अनुष्ठान (external forms of consciousness)। 'सत्यकामाः' = सत्य के अभीप्सु। कर्म = यात्रा का आरम्भ — ज्ञान = यात्रा की पूर्णता।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says seer-perceived rituals = external forms of consciousness. 'Satya-kāmāḥ' = aspirants of truth. Karma = the beginning of the journey — knowledge = the journey's completion.
aurobindo.ins: The rituals are consciousness in its outer form — real, seer-perceived, valid. Start there if that's where you are. But know that the path continues — from outer ritual to inner knowledge, from the world of good deeds to the ocean of Brahman.

dp.q: 🔍 The triple bridge: 3.1.5-7 = 2.2.8, 10-11
dp.a:
तृतीय मुण्डक तिहरी पुनरुक्ति से खुलता है — द्वितीय मुण्डक के मन्त्रों का व्यापक सेतु बनाता है। तीन दोहराए गए मन्त्र: (1) 3.1.5 = 2.2.10: तप-सृष्टि क्रम। (2) 3.1.6 = 2.2.11: सर्वज्ञ, सर्ववैभवी ब्रह्म + 'तदेतत्सत्यम्।' (3) 3.1.7 = 2.2.8: सत्य-प्रेमियों के लिए कर्म-मार्ग। उपलब्धि: तृतीय मुण्डक द्वितीय की सम्पूर्ण शिक्षा — ज्ञान-मार्ग (तप/ब्रह्म) और कर्म-मार्ग (अनुष्ठान/ऋषि) दोनों — को वहन करके आगे बढ़ता है। फिर अपनी अद्वितीय और चरम शिक्षाएँ प्रस्तुत करता है: दो पक्षी (3.1.1-2), सुवर्ण-पुरुष (3.1.3), ज्ञानी का चित्र (3.1.4), और खण्ड 2 में हृदय-ग्रन्थि छेदन, नदी-सागर उपमा, 'ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मैव भवति।'

Eng: The third Muṇḍaka opens with a triple repetition of verses from the second Muṇḍaka, creating a comprehensive bridge: The three repeated verses: (1) 3.1.5 = 2.2.10: 'tapasā cīyate brahma...' — the creation-through-tapas sequence. (2) 3.1.6 = 2.2.11: 'yaḥ sarva-jñaḥ sarva-vit...' — the all-knowing, all-glorious Brahman + 'tat etat satyam.' (3) 3.1.7 = 2.2.8: 'tat etat satyam... tāni ācaratha...' — the ritual path for lovers of truth. What this achieves: the third Muṇḍaka begins by carrying forward the COMPLETE teaching of the second — both the knowledge-path (tapas/Brahman) and the action-path (rituals/seers). It then advances to its own unique and culminating teachings: the two birds (3.1.1-2), the golden Puruṣa (3.1.3), the knower's portrait (3.1.4), and — in Khanda 2 — the cutting of the heart-knot, the river-ocean simile, and the climactic 'brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati.' The ordering of the mantras: note that in Khanda 1, mantras 1-4 contain the NEW teachings (two birds, golden Puruṣa, knower's portrait), while mantras 5-7 are repetitions. Some editions reverse this ordering. The exact sequence varies across recensions, but the content is identical.

dp.q: 🔍 'Satya-kāmāḥ' — the qualification for the path
dp.a:
'सत्यकामाः' सम्बोधन बताता है कि यह उपदेश किसके लिए है। सत्यकाम कौन? जो सत्य (reality/truth) की कामना (desire) करते हैं — न धन, न शक्ति, न स्वर्गीय भोग — बल्कि सत्य। छान्दोग्य का सत्यकाम (4.4): प्रसिद्ध शिष्य सत्यकाम जाबाल — जिसका नाम ही 'सत्य-प्रेमी' — जब गोत्र पूछा तो ईमानदारी से बोला: 'मेरे पिता का नाम नहीं जानता।' गुरु गौतम ने ठीक इसी सत्यनिष्ठा से प्रभावित होकर दीक्षा दी। पात्रता: कर्म-मार्ग भी उदासीन, आलसी या आत्मवंचित के लिए नहीं — 'सत्यकामाः' के लिए। सत्य-उन्मुखता बिना अनुष्ठान खोखले — 1.2.7 की 'छिद्रयुक्त नौकाएँ।'

Eng: The address 'satya-kāmāḥ' ('lovers of truth') specifies WHO this instruction is for: Who are the satya-kāmāḥ? Those who desire (kāma) truth (satya) — not wealth, not power, not even heavenly pleasures, but TRUTH. This is not just anyone — it is a specific class of seekers whose primary motivation is the desire for reality, for what IS, for the ultimate truth behind appearances. The Chāndogya's Satyakāma (4.4): the famous student Satyakāma Jābāla — whose very name means 'lover of truth' — is the archetype. When asked his lineage (gotra), he answered honestly: 'I do not know my father's name; my mother told me she had many masters.' The teacher Gautama accepted him precisely because of this truthfulness: 'A non-Brāhmaṇa would not speak thus. Bring the fuel, dear one; I will initiate you.' The qualification: the path of rituals is not for the indifferent, the lazy, or the self-deceived — it is for 'lovers of truth.' Even the action-path requires sincerity and truth-seeking to be effective. Without that inner orientation toward truth, rituals become empty gestures — the 'leaky boats' of 1.2.7.

sk: यथा नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः समुद्रेऽस्तं गच्छन्ति नामरूपे विहाय तथा विद्वान्नामरूपाद्विमुक्तः परात्परं पुरुषमुपैति दिव्यम् ||
ro: yathā · nadyaḥ · syandamānāḥ · samudre · astaṁ · gacchanti · nāma-rūpe · vihāya · tathā · vidvān · nāma-rūpāt · vimuktaḥ · parāt · paraṁ · puruṣam · upaiti · divyam ||
hi: जैसे (यथा) नदियाँ (nadyaḥ) स्यन्दमानाः (flowing / बहती हुईं) समुद्र (ocean) में अस्तं गच्छन्ति (disappear / विलीन हो जाती हैं) — नामरूपे विहाय (having abandoned name and form / नाम-रूप छोड़कर) — वैसे ही (तथा) विद्वान् (the wise one / ज्ञानी) नामरूपात् विमुक्तः (freed from name and form) — परात्परम् (beyond the beyond / परे-से-भी-परे) दिव्यम् पुरुषम् (the divine Person) उपैति (attains / प्राप्त करता है)।
en: Just as (yathā) rivers (nadyaḥ), flowing (syandamānāḥ), disappear (astaṁ gacchanti) into the ocean (samudre), abandoning (vihāya) name and form (nāma-rūpe) — so (tathā) the wise one (vidvān), freed (vimuktaḥ) from name and form (nāma-rūpāt), attains (upaiti) the divine (divyam) Person (puruṣam) who is beyond the beyond (parāt param).
gr:
व्याकरण: यथा ... तथा — उपमा-सूचक (simile construction) — 'जैसे ... वैसे ही।' नद्यः स्यन्दमानाः — 'नद्यः' = नदी का प्रथमा बहुवचन; 'स्यन्दमानाः' = √स्यन्द् (बहना) — शानच् प्रत्यय (present participle middle) — 'बहती हुईं।' समुद्रे अस्तं गच्छन्ति — 'समुद्रे' = सप्तमी; 'अस्तम् गच्छन्ति' = 'अस्त हो जाती हैं / विलीन हो जाती हैं' — सूर्यास्त की भाँति — दिखना बन्द, नष्ट नहीं। नामरूपे विहाय — 'विहाय' = वि + √हा (त्यागना) — ल्यबन्त (absolutive) — 'त्यागकर' — नदियाँ अपने नाम (गंगा, यमुना) और रूप (चौड़ी, सँकरी) छोड़कर 'सागर' हो जाती हैं। परात् परं पुरुषम् — 'परात् परम्' = 'परे-से-भी-परे' — सर्वातीत — सभी श्रेणियों से परे। दिव्यम् = √दिव् (चमकना) — 'स्वयंप्रकाश / दिव्य।' यह मुण्डक की सर्वाधिक सुन्दर और प्रभावशाली उपमाओं में से एक।
Eng: The river-ocean simile — liberation as merging. 'Syandamānāḥ' (middle participle of √syand = to flow). 'Astaṁ gacchanti' = disappear/set (like the sun — not destroyed but absorbed). 'Nāma-rūpe vihāya' (absolutive of vi+√hā) = having abandoned name and form. 'Parāt paraṁ' = beyond the beyond — transcending all categories. 'Divyam' (√div) = self-luminous/divine.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — नदियाँ समुद्र में मिलकर 'नदी' नहीं रहतीं — नाम (गंगा, यमुना) और रूप (चौड़ी, सँकरी) खो देती हैं — केवल 'समुद्र' रहता है। वैसे ही जीव ब्रह्म में मिलकर 'जीव' नहीं रहता — नाम-रूप-उपाधि (name-form-limiting adjuncts) खो देता है — केवल ब्रह्म। यही मोक्ष = पूर्ण ऐक्य (absolute identity)।
advaita.en: Shankara says rivers merging into the ocean cease to be 'rivers' — they lose name (Gaṅgā, Yamunā) and form (wide, narrow) — only 'ocean' remains. Similarly, the jīva merging into Brahman ceases to be 'jīva' — loses name-form-limiting adjuncts — only Brahman. This is mokṣa = absolute identity.
advaita.ins: The Gaṅgā flows and flows — and then it reaches the ocean. And what happens? The Gaṅgā disappears. Not destroyed — but absorbed. It's all ocean now. There is no 'Gaṅgā' in the ocean — just ocean. That's liberation. You don't die — you become infinite. Your name and form dissolve into what you always were.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — नदी समुद्र में मिलती है — किन्तु जल (water) जल ही रहता है — नष्ट (destroyed) नहीं होता। वैसे ही जीव भगवान् में मिलता है — किन्तु जीव (soul) जीव ही रहता है — नष्ट नहीं — सायुज्य (intimate union) — ऐक्य (identity) नहीं।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says the river merges into the ocean — but water remains water — it is not destroyed. Similarly, the jīva merges into God — but the soul remains a soul — not destroyed — intimate union (sāyujya) — not identity.
vishisht.ins: The river reaches the ocean and loses its name — it's no longer 'Gaṅgā.' But the water is still water. It hasn't become something else — it has found its home. Your soul finds its home in God — losing the small name and form, but remaining real, conscious, blissful, resting in God's infinite presence.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — नदी-सागर = व्यक्तिगत चेतना (individual consciousness) विश्व-चेतना (universal consciousness) में विलीन। 'नामरूपे विहाय' = सीमित पहचान (limited identity) छोड़कर। 'परात्परं पुरुषम्' = सच्चिदानन्द — चेतना का विस्तार (expansion), विनाश (destruction) नहीं।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says river-ocean = individual consciousness merges into universal consciousness. 'Nāma-rūpe vihāya' = abandoning limited identity. 'Parāt paraṁ puruṣam' = Sat-Chit-Ānanda — expansion of consciousness, not destruction.
aurobindo.ins: The river doesn't die in the ocean — it expands. It was always ocean-water; now it knows it. Your consciousness doesn't die in Brahman — it expands beyond all names and forms into the infinite. You don't lose yourself — you find what you always were, beneath the name and form.

dp.q: 🔍 The river-ocean simile — merging, not annihilation
dp.a:
नदी-सागर उपमा भारतीय दर्शन की सर्वाधिक उद्धृत और विवादित छवियों में से एक है। छवि: नदियाँ सागर की ओर बहती हैं — सागर पहुँचकर 'विलीन' हो जाती हैं — अपने व्यक्तिगत नाम (गंगा, यमुना) और रूप (चौड़ी, सँकरी, स्वच्छ, मटमैली) छोड़कर। तीन व्याख्याएँ: (1) अद्वैत: नदी की व्यक्तिगतता सदा भ्रामक थी — नदी सदा सागर-जल ही था। 'विलय' = अस्थायी उपाधियों (नाम-रूप) का हटना। कुछ वास्तविक न खोया, न पाया। (2) विशिष्टाद्वैत: नदी सागर में मिलती है — किन्तु जल जल ही रहता है — नष्ट नहीं। जीव भगवान् में — किन्तु चेतन इकाई बना रहता है — सायुज्य, ऐक्य नहीं। (3) श्री अरविन्द: विलय = विस्तार, विनाश नहीं। नदी की चेतना, जो नदी-तट तक सीमित थी, अब अनन्त में व्याप्त। प्रश्न-उपनिषद् समानान्तर (6.5): पुरुष की सोलह 'कलाओं' का विलय — नदियों-सा सागर में।

Eng: The river-ocean simile is one of the most widely quoted and most debated images in Indian philosophy: The image: rivers flow toward the ocean. Upon reaching the ocean, they 'disappear' (astaṁ gacchanti) — losing their individual names (Gaṅgā, Yamunā) and forms (wide, narrow, clear, muddy). Once in the ocean, you can't point to the 'Gaṅgā part' of the ocean or the 'Yamunā part' — there is only ocean. The three readings: (1) Advaita: the river's individuality was always illusory. The river was always ocean-water flowing in a temporary channel. 'Merging' = the removal of the temporary channel (nāma-rūpa/upādhis). Nothing real is lost; nothing real is gained. The river-ness was never real; the ocean-ness was always there. (2) Viśiṣṭādvaita: the river genuinely merges but the water remains water. The soul's individuality is not illusory but real — upon liberation, the soul enters God and shares His qualities (sārūpya), but remains a distinct conscious entity. The ocean contains the river but doesn't annihilate it. (3) Sri Aurobindo: merging = expansion, not annihilation. The river doesn't disappear — it becomes the ocean. Its consciousness, formerly limited to a river-bed, now pervades the infinite. Liberation is not loss of individuality but expansion to universality. The Praśna parallel (6.5): the Praśna uses the same image for the dissolution of the sixteen 'parts' of the Person — they merge into the Puruṣa as rivers into the ocean.

dp.q: 🔍 'Parāt paraṁ puruṣam divyam' — the Person beyond the beyond
dp.a:
'परात् परं पुरुषम् दिव्यम्' ('परे-से-भी-परे दिव्य पुरुष') — मुक्त आत्मा का गन्तव्य। परात् परम् = 'परे से भी परे' — पुरुष सभी श्रेणियों से — प्रकट जगत् (क्षर) से, अव्यक्त (अक्षर) से, 'परे' से भी — अतीत है। दिव्यम् = √दिव् (चमकना) — स्वयंप्रकाश — न सूर्य से, न चन्द्रमा से, न अग्नि से — स्वयं चमकता है (कठ 2.2.15, मुण्डक 2.2.10)। पुरुषम् = 'व्यक्ति' — अमूर्त शक्ति या शून्य नहीं — चेतन, ज्योतिर्मय, व्यक्तिगत उपस्थिति। गन्तव्य: नदियाँ यहीं जाती हैं — ज्ञानी यही प्राप्त करता है — कोई अवधारणा नहीं, कोई अवस्था नहीं, कोई शून्य नहीं — एक पुरुष: ज्योतिर्मय, दिव्य, सब 'परे' से भी परे।

Eng: The closing phrase 'parāt paraṁ puruṣam divyam' ('the divine Person beyond the beyond') describes the destination of the liberated soul: Parāt param = 'beyond the beyond': this phrase (used also at 2.1.2: 'akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ') indicates that the Puruṣa transcends ALL categories — even the highest categories of Vedāntic thought. He is beyond the manifest world (kṣara), beyond the unmanifest (akṣara), beyond even the 'beyond.' Divyam = 'divine / self-luminous': from √div (to shine). The Puruṣa shines by its own light — it needs no external illumination. It is not seen by the sun's light, or the moon's, or fire's — it shines, and everything else shines after it (cf. Kaṭha 2.2.15, Muṇḍaka 2.2.10). Puruṣam = 'the Person': not an abstraction, not a force, not an 'it' — a Person (Puruṣa). The ultimate reality is personal — it has awareness, glory, and self-luminosity. This is not pantheism (everything is God) or deism (God is distant) but something subtler: the ultimate reality is a conscious, luminous, personal Presence that transcends all categories yet is intimately accessible. The destination: this is where the rivers go. This is what the wise one attains. Not a concept, not a state, not a void — but a Person: luminous, divine, beyond all beyonds.

sk: स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति नास्याब्रह्मवित्कुले भवति तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानं गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तोऽमृतो भवति ||
ro: saḥ · yaḥ · ha · vai · tat · paramaṁ · brahma · veda · brahma · eva · bhavati · na · asya · a-brahma-vit · kule · bhavati · tarati · śokaṁ · tarati · pāpmānaṁ · guhā-granthibhyaḥ · vimuktaḥ · amṛtaḥ · bhavati ||
hi: जो (यः) वह (सः) परमं ब्रह्म (supreme Brahman) को वेद (knows / जानता है) — वह ब्रह्मैव भवति (becomes Brahman itself / ब्रह्म ही हो जाता है)। उसके कुल (family / वंश) में कोई अब्रह्मवित् (non-knower of Brahman / ब्रह्म-अज्ञानी) नहीं भवति (is born)। वह शोकम् (sorrow) तरति (crosses beyond / पार करता है), पाप्मानम् (sin / evil) तरति (crosses beyond), गुहा-ग्रन्थिभ्यः (from the knots of the heart / हृदय-गुहा की गाँठों से) विमुक्तः (freed) — अमृतः भवति (becomes immortal)।
en: He who knows (veda) that supreme Brahman (paramaṁ brahma) — becomes Brahman itself (brahmaiva bhavati). In his family (kule), no one is born (bhavati) who does not know Brahman (a-brahma-vit). He crosses beyond (tarati) sorrow (śokam), crosses beyond sin (pāpmānam); freed (vimuktaḥ) from the knots of the heart (guhā-granthibhyaḥ), he becomes immortal (amṛtaḥ bhavati).

ws.e: from the knots of the heart-cave

gr:
व्याकरण: स यो ह वै — 'सः यः' = 'वह जो'; 'ह वै' = बलप्रदान (emphatic particles) — 'निश्चय ही' — उपनिषदों में महत्वपूर्ण घोषणाओं से पूर्व प्रयुक्त। तत् परमं ब्रह्म वेद — 'वेद' = √विद् (जानना) — लट् (present) — 'जानता है' — यहाँ 'जानना' = बौद्धिक ज्ञान नहीं, प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव। ब्रह्मैव भवति = ब्रह्म + एव (ही) + भवति — 'ब्रह्म ही हो जाता है' — सर्वाधिक क्रान्तिकारी कथन — ज्ञानी ब्रह्म के बारे में नहीं जानता, ब्रह्म हो जाता है — ज्ञान = अस्तित्व। न अस्य अब्रह्मवित् कुले भवति — 'अब्रह्मवित्' = अ + ब्रह्म + विद् — 'ब्रह्म को न जानने वाला' — उसके वंश में कोई ब्रह्म-अज्ञानी नहीं जन्मता। तरति शोकं तरति पाप्मानम् — 'तरति' = √तृ (तैरना/पार करना) — शोक और पाप दोनों 'पार' — भावनात्मक और नैतिक बन्धन दोनों से मुक्ति। गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यः विमुक्तः — 'गुहा' = गुफा / हृदय-गुहा; 'ग्रन्थि' = गाँठ — 2.1.10 (अविद्या-ग्रन्थि) को वापस लाता है — अविद्या, काम, कर्म की गाँठें कटती हैं। अमृतः भवति — 'अमृत होता है' — बाह्य पुरस्कार नहीं, आत्मा सदा अमर था — ज्ञानी इसे पहचानता है।
Eng: The Muṇḍaka's climactic declaration. 'Ha vai' — emphatic particles for momentous statements. 'Brahmaiva bhavati' — the knower BECOMES Brahman (knowing = being). 'Na asya abrahma-vit kule bhavati' — knowledge radiates through lineage. 'Tarati' (√tṛ) = crosses beyond (both sorrow and sin). 'Guhā-granthibhyaḥ' echoes 2.1.10 — the heart-knots (ignorance, desire, karma) are cut. 'Amṛtaḥ bhavati' = becomes immortal — not gains immortality, but realises it.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — 'ब्रह्मैव भवति' = ज्ञानी = ब्रह्म ही। यह 'बनना' (becoming) नहीं = 'पहचानना' (recognising)। जीव सदा ब्रह्म था — अज्ञान ने ढँक रखा था — ज्ञान से अज्ञान-आवरण (veil of ignorance) हटा — 'ब्रह्मैव भवति' = 'ब्रह्म ही है, ऐसा जानता है।' 'गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तः' = हृदय-गाँठें (heart-knots) — अहंकार, काम, कर्म — कट जाती हैं।
advaita.en: Shankara says 'brahmaiva bhavati' = the knower = Brahman itself. This is not 'becoming' but 'recognising.' The jīva was always Brahman — ignorance covered it — knowledge removes the veil — 'brahmaiva bhavati' = 'knows oneself to BE Brahman.' 'Guhā-granthibhyaḥ vimuktaḥ' = heart-knots — ego, desire, karma — are cut.
advaita.ins: You don't BECOME Brahman — you RECOGNISE that you always WERE Brahman. The knot of ignorance was hiding it. When the knot is cut, what's revealed? Not something new — something that was always there. You ARE Brahman. You always were. The knower of Brahman becomes Brahman — because the knower was never anything else.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — 'ब्रह्मैव भवति' = ब्रह्म-सदृश (Brahman-like) हो जाता है — ब्रह्म के गुणों (qualities) को प्राप्त करता है — ऐक्य (absolute identity) नहीं — सारूप्य (similarity) + सायुज्य (union)। 'कुले अब्रह्मवित् न भवति' = ज्ञानी का वंश (lineage) भी धन्य (blessed) — भगवद्-कृपा (God's grace) परिवार में प्रवाहित होती है।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says 'brahmaiva bhavati' = becomes Brahman-LIKE — attains Brahman's qualities — not absolute identity but similarity (sārūpya) + union (sāyujya). 'Kule abrahma-vit na bhavati' = the knower's lineage is blessed — God's grace flows through the family.
vishisht.ins: The knower of Brahman becomes like Brahman — sharing His qualities, His immortality, His freedom from sorrow. Not identical — but so close that the distinction almost vanishes. And the grace flows through the family — when one person truly knows God, the light spreads to everyone around them.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — 'ब्रह्मैव भवति' = चेतना-रूपान्तर (transformation of consciousness) — व्यक्तिगत चेतना (individual consciousness) विश्व-चेतना (universal consciousness) में रूपान्तरित। 'गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यो विमुक्तः' = अहंकार (ego) की गाँठें — चेतना को सीमित करने वाली — कट जाती हैं। 'अमृतः' = चेतना = सदा अमर — मृत्यु = भ्रम (illusion)।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says 'brahmaiva bhavati' = transformation of consciousness — individual consciousness is transformed into universal consciousness. 'Guhā-granthibhyaḥ vimuktaḥ' = the ego-knots — which limit consciousness — are cut. 'Amṛtaḥ' = consciousness = ever immortal — death = illusion.
aurobindo.ins: The knower of Brahman doesn't just learn about Brahman — they BECOME Brahman. Consciousness transforms: what was individual becomes universal, what was limited becomes infinite. The knots of the ego are cut — and what's left is immortal consciousness, free from sorrow, free from sin, shining like gold.

dp.q: 🔍 'Brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati' — the knower becomes Brahman
dp.a:
'ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मैव भवति' — सम्पूर्ण उपनिषद्-साहित्य की सबसे महत्वपूर्ण घोषणाओं में से एक। क्या कहती है: जो ब्रह्म को सच में जानता है, वह ब्रह्म को केवल समझता ही नहीं, उसके पास आता ही नहीं — ब्रह्म हो जाता है। ज्ञान और अस्तित्व एक। तीन व्याख्याएँ: (1) अद्वैत: 'हो जाना' = पहचानना कि सदा ब्रह्म ही था — जीव की पृथक् सत्ता सदा भ्रामक (माया) — 'हो जाना' = अज्ञान-निवृत्ति, वास्तविक रूपान्तर नहीं। (2) विशिष्टाद्वैत: 'हो जाना' = ब्रह्म-सदृश — ब्रह्म के गुण (शोक-मुक्ति, अमरत्व, आनन्द) प्राप्त — सायुज्य (intimate union) — ऐक्य नहीं। (3) श्री अरविन्द: 'हो जाना' = चेतना-रूपान्तर — व्यक्तिगत चेतना विश्व-चेतना में — वास्तविक रूपान्तर (न केवल अनावृत्ति) — विनाश नहीं — जो सदा सम्भाव्य था, उसकी पूर्णतम अभिव्यक्ति। चार महावाक्यों में नहीं: औपचारिक रूप से 'तत्त्वमसि', 'अहं ब्रह्मास्मि', 'प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म', 'अयमात्मा ब्रह्म' — किन्तु 'ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मैव भवति' एक वास्तविक पाँचवाँ महावाक्य — सम्भवतः सबसे प्रत्यक्ष और सबसे क्रान्तिकारी।

Eng: The declaration 'brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati' ('the knower of Brahman becomes Brahman itself') is one of the most important statements in the entire Upanishadic corpus: What it says: the person who truly knows Brahman does not merely understand it, approach it, or relate to it — they become it. Knowledge and being are identical. To know Brahman fully IS to be Brahman. Three interpretations: (1) Advaita: 'becomes Brahman' = recognises that one was ALWAYS Brahman. The jīva's separate identity was always illusory (māyā). 'Becoming' = the removal of ignorance, not a real transformation. Nothing changes except that the veil lifts. (2) Viśiṣṭādvaita: 'becomes Brahman' = becomes Brahman-like — attains Brahman's qualities (freedom from sorrow, immortality, bliss) through intimate union. The soul doesn't literally become Brahman but shares Brahman's nature to the fullest extent possible while remaining a distinct conscious entity. (3) Sri Aurobindo: 'becomes Brahman' = consciousness transforms — the individual consciousness expands and is transmuted into universal/supramental consciousness. This is a real transformation (not just unveiling) but not annihilation — it is the fullest expression of what the individual always potentially was. Not one of the four mahāvākyas: formally, the four mahāvākyas are: 'tat tvam asi' (Chāndogya), 'aham brahmāsmi' (Bṛhadāraṇyaka), 'prajñānaṁ brahma' (Aitareya), 'ayam ātmā brahma' (Māṇḍūkya). But 'brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati' functions as a de facto fifth — and is arguably the most direct and the most radical of them all.

dp.q: 🔍 The cutting of the heart-knots — 'guhā-granthibhyaḥ vimuktaḥ'
dp.a:
'गुहाग्रन्थिभ्यः विमुक्तः' — मुण्डक की दो केन्द्रीय छवियों — गुहा (हृदय-गुफा) और ग्रन्थि (गाँठ) — को एकत्र करता है। गाँठें क्या हैं? हृदय-ग्रन्थियाँ — मूलभूत आसक्तियाँ और भ्रान्त पहचान जो आत्मा को संसार से बाँधती हैं: (1) अविद्या-ग्रन्थि — अपने स्वरूप का मूलभूत अज्ञान। (2) काम-ग्रन्थि — विषयों, अनुभवों, फलों की तृष्णा। (3) कर्म-ग्रन्थि — कर्तृत्व और फल से तादात्म्य। कठ समानान्तर (2.3.15): 'यदा सर्वे प्रभिद्यन्ते हृदयस्येह ग्रन्थयः / अथ मर्त्योऽमृतो भवति' — 'जब सब हृदय-ग्रन्थियाँ यहीं छिन्न हो जाती हैं — मर्त्य अमृत हो जाता है।' कैसे कटती हैं? ज्ञान (प्रत्यक्ष अनुभूति) से — गाँठें धीरे-धीरे नहीं खुलतीं, 'काटी' जाती हैं — जैसे तीक्ष्ण धार से रस्सी। दो पक्षियों से सम्बन्ध: गाँठें ही 'खाने वाले पक्षी' को खाते रखती हैं — गाँठ कटते ही खाने वाला ऊपर देखता है, देखने वाले को पहचानता है — खाना बन्द, शोक बन्द — पहचान सीमित से असीमित में।

Eng: The phrase 'guhā-granthibhyaḥ vimuktaḥ' ('freed from the knots of the heart-cave') brings together two of the Muṇḍaka's central images — the guhā (cave of the heart) and the granthi (knot): What are the knots? The 'knots of the heart' (hṛdaya-granthayaḥ) are the fundamental attachments and misidentifications that bind the Self to saṁsāra: (1) The knot of ignorance (avidyā-granthi) — the fundamental not-knowing of one's own nature. 'I don't know who I am.' (2) The knot of desire (kāma-granthi) — the craving for objects, experiences, and outcomes. 'I want.' (3) The knot of action (karma-granthi) — the identification with one's actions and their results. 'I am the doer; I deserve the fruit.' The Kaṭha parallel (2.3.15): 'yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ / atha martyo'mṛto bhavati' — 'When all the knots of the heart are cut HERE, the mortal becomes immortal.' How the knots are cut: through knowledge (jñāna) — specifically, the direct realisation 'brahma-vid brahmaiva bhavati.' The knots are not gradually loosened but 'cut' (bhidyante / vimuktaḥ) — like a rope cut with a sharp blade. The blade is knowledge. The knots cannot be untied by effort alone — they must be cut by the sharp edge of direct insight. The connection to the two birds: the knots are what keep the 'eating bird' eating.
