When the knots are cut, the eating bird looks up, sees the watching bird, and recognises its true identity. The eating stops. Sorrow stops. Identity shifts from the limited to the unlimited.

sk: तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम् क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रिया ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः स्वयं जुह्वत एकर्षिं श्रद्धयन्तः एतद्ब्रह्मविद्यां ह वै ब्रह्मनिष्ठोऽथ विद्वानुपसन्नं यथाविधिं पुरुषं वेदयेत ||
ro: tat · etat · ṛcā · abhyuktam · kriyāvantaḥ · śrotriyāḥ · brahma-niṣṭhāḥ · svayaṁ · juhvataḥ · eka-ṛṣiṁ · śraddhayantaḥ · etat · brahma-vidyāṁ · ha · vai · brahma-niṣṭhaḥ · atha · vidvān · upasannaṁ · yathā-vidhiṁ · puruṣaṁ · vedayet ||
hi: वह यह ऋचा (Vedic verse) से अभ्युक्त (declared / कहा गया) है — क्रियावन्तः (those engaged in action / कर्मनिष्ठ), श्रोत्रियाः (learned in the Vedas / श्रुति-विद्), ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः (devoted to Brahman / ब्रह्मपरायण) — जो स्वयं जुह्वतः (offering oblations to the one Seer / एक ऋषि को आहुति देते हैं) श्रद्धा से (with faith / श्रद्धापूर्वक) — इस ब्रह्मविद्या (brahma-vidyā / knowledge of Brahman) को वह ब्रह्मनिष्ठ (Brahman-devoted), विद्वान् (wise one) — उपसन्नम् (one who has duly approached / विधिपूर्वक उपसन्न) पुरुष को यथाविधि (according to rule / विधि-अनुसार) वेदयेत् (should teach / बताए)।
en: This is declared (abhyuktam) by the Vedic verse (ṛcā): those who are active (kriyāvantaḥ), learned in the Vedas (śrotriyāḥ), devoted to Brahman (brahma-niṣṭhāḥ), who themselves offer oblations (svayaṁ juhvataḥ) to the one Seer (eka-ṛṣim) with faith (śraddhayantaḥ) — to them should this brahma-vidyā [be taught]. Indeed, the wise one (vidvān), devoted to Brahman (brahma-niṣṭhaḥ), should teach (vedayet) the Person (puruṣam) to one who has duly approached (upasannam) according to rule (yathā-vidhim).

ws.h: आहुति देने वाले / हवन करने वाले
विधिपूर्वक उपसन्न / शिष्य जो समीप आया

gr:
व्याकरण: तदेतत् ऋचा अभ्युक्तम् — 'ऋचा' = तृतीया एकवचन (instrumental) — 'ऋचा के द्वारा'; 'अभ्युक्तम्' = अभि + √वच् (कहना) — 'कहा गया / घोषित।' क्रियावन्तः श्रोत्रियाः ब्रह्मनिष्ठाः — योग्य गुरु के तीन गुण: (1) क्रियावान् = कर्मशील; (2) श्रोत्रिय = श्रुति + इय — 'वेदपारंगत'; (3) ब्रह्मनिष्ठ = ब्रह्म + निष्ठा (स्थिरता) — 'ब्रह्म में स्थित।' स्वयं जुह्वतः एकर्षिम् — 'जुह्वतः' = √हु (आहुति देना) — शतृ बहुवचन — 'स्वयं आहुति देने वाले'; 'एकर्षिम्' = एक + ऋषि — 'एक द्रष्टा' = ब्रह्म। श्रद्धयन्तः = श्रद्धा + यत् — 'श्रद्धापूर्वक।' उपसन्नम् = उप + √सद् (बैठना/पास जाना) — 'जो विधिपूर्वक गुरु के पास आया' — 1.2.12 (समित्पाणि) की प्रतिध्वनि। यथाविधि = यथा + विधि — 'विधि-अनुसार' — गुरु-शिष्य परम्परा का पालन। वेदयेत् = √विद् (जानना) का णिजन्त (causative) — विधिलिङ् (optative) — 'ज्ञान कराए / सिखाए।' वृत्त बन्द होता है: मुण्डक आरम्भ (1.1.1-2) में गुरु-परम्परा (ब्रह्मा → अथर्वा → अङ्गिर → सत्यवाह → अङ्गिरस् → शौनक) — अब अन्त में इस परम्परा की निरन्तरता की पुष्टि।
Eng: The closing transmission protocol. 'Ṛcā abhyuktam' = declared by the Vedic verse. Three qualifications of the teacher: kriyāvān (active), śrotriya (Veda-learned), brahma-niṣṭha (established in Brahman). 'Eka-ṛṣim' = the one Seer (Brahman). 'Upasannam' (upa + √sad) = one who has duly approached — echoing 1.2.12. 'Vedayet' = causative optative of √vid — 'should make known / teach.' The Muṇḍaka's circle closes.

advaita.h: शंकर कहते हैं — ब्रह्मविद्या = केवल अधिकारी (qualified) को ही दी जाए। गुरु = (1) क्रियावान् (active), (2) श्रोत्रिय (Veda-learned), (3) ब्रह्मनिष्ठ (established in Brahman)। शिष्य = उपसन्न (duly approached) — समित्पाणि (1.2.12)। 'यथाविधि' = गुरु-शिष्य परम्परा (teacher-student lineage) का पालन।
advaita.en: Shankara says brahma-vidyā should be given only to the qualified. The guru must be (1) kriyāvān (active), (2) śrotriya (Veda-learned), (3) brahma-niṣṭha (established in Brahman). The student must be upasanna (duly approached) — samit-pāṇi (1.2.12). 'Yathā-vidhi' = following the teacher-student lineage.
advaita.ins: The highest knowledge isn't sold in a market or broadcast on a stage. It flows from qualified teacher to qualified student, through proper channels, according to rule. The teacher must be learned, established, and active. The student must approach with humility and readiness. Then — and only then — the Person is revealed.

vishisht.h: रामानुज कहते हैं — ब्रह्मविद्या = भक्ति-ज्ञान (devotional knowledge) — केवल योग्य शिष्य (qualified student) को — योग्य गुरु (qualified teacher) द्वारा। 'एकर्षिम् जुह्वतः' = एक परमात्मा (one Supreme Lord) को आहुति देने वाले — भगवद्-भक्त (devotees of God)। 'उपसन्नम्' = शरणागत (surrendered) शिष्य।
vishisht.en: Ramanuja says brahma-vidyā = devotional knowledge — only to qualified students by qualified teachers. 'Eka-ṛṣim juhvataḥ' = those who offer oblations to the one Supreme Lord — devotees of God. 'Upasannam' = the surrendered student.
vishisht.ins: This knowledge is sacred — not to be given casually. The teacher must be learned, devoted, and active. The student must approach with surrender and faith. Then the teacher reveals the Person — the one Lord who is the Seer behind all seeing, the one reality behind all the rituals, all the knowledge, all the devotion.

aurobindo.h: श्री अरविन्द कहते हैं — ब्रह्मविद्या = चेतना का ज्ञान (knowledge of consciousness) — व्यक्तिगत संचारण (personal transmission) से। 'एकर्षिम्' = एक चेतना (one consciousness) — जो सब ऋषियों (seers) में देखती है। गुरु-शिष्य सम्बन्ध = चेतना-संचारण (consciousness-transmission) का माध्यम।
aurobindo.en: Sri Aurobindo says brahma-vidyā = knowledge of consciousness — through personal transmission. 'Eka-ṛṣim' = the one consciousness that sees through all seers. The guru-student relationship = the medium of consciousness-transmission.
aurobindo.ins: This knowledge can't be downloaded — it's transmitted, person to person, consciousness to consciousness. The teacher who is established in Brahman lights the flame in the student who is ready. The one Seer — who looks through every pair of eyes — recognises Itself in both teacher and student. That recognition IS the teaching.

dp.q: 🔍 The guru-śiṣya paramparā — sacred transmission
dp.a:
यह समापन मन्त्र गुरु-शिष्य परम्परा के महत्व की पुष्टि करता है। योग्य गुरु: (1) क्रियावान् — कर्मशील (संसार से विरत नहीं) — ज्ञान को जीने वाला। (2) श्रोत्रिय — वेदपारंगत — बौद्धिक आधार। (3) ब्रह्मनिष्ठ — ब्रह्म में स्थित — प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव, केवल पुस्तकीय ज्ञान नहीं। योग्य शिष्य: उपसन्न — विधिपूर्वक गुरु के पास आया — विनम्रता, तत्परता, ईमानदारी। मुण्डक का अपना आरम्भ (1.2.12-13): 'समित्पाणि' (हाथ में समिधा), 'प्रशान्तचित्त', 'शमान्वित।' विधि: यथाविधि — परम्परा-अनुसार — सामान्य, आकस्मिक, सार्वजनिक शिक्षा नहीं — पवित्र कृत्य। मुण्डक का वृत्त: उपनिषद् ब्रह्मा → अथर्वा → अङ्गिर → सत्यवाह → अङ्गिरस् → शौनक परम्परा से आरम्भ हुआ — अब अन्त में इस परम्परा की निरन्तरता की पुष्टि — हर पीढ़ी का ब्रह्मज्ञानी अगली पीढ़ी के योग्य शिष्य को सिखाए।

Eng: This closing mantra affirms the importance of the guru-śiṣya paramparā (teacher-student lineage) for the transmission of brahma-vidyā: The qualified teacher must be: (1) Kriyāvān (active): not a recluse but engaged with the world — living the knowledge, not just knowing it. (2) Śrotriya (Veda-learned): having studied the Vedas and the Upanishads under a proper teacher — possessing the intellectual framework. (3) Brahma-niṣṭha (established in Brahman): having direct experience of Brahman — not just book-knowledge but living realisation. The qualified student must be: Upasanna (duly approached): having come to the teacher properly — with humility, sincerity, and readiness. The Muṇḍaka's own opening (1.2.12-13) describes this: the student must be 'samit-pāṇi' (with fuel in hand — the traditional mark of readiness), 'praśānta-citta' (with pacified mind), and 'śama-anvita' (possessed of self-control). The method: Yathā-vidhi (according to rule): the teaching follows established procedure — it is not casual, not improvised, not public. It is a sacred act, governed by tradition. The Muṇḍaka's circle: the Upanishad opened with the lineage Brahmā → Atharvā → Aṅgir → Satyavāha → Aṅgiras → Śaunaka. It closes by affirming that this lineage must continue — each generation's Brahman-knower must teach the next generation's qualified student. The chain is unbroken.

dp.q: 🔍 'Eka-ṛṣim' — Brahman as the one Seer
dp.a:
'एकर्षिम्' ('एक द्रष्टा') — ब्रह्म का एक सुन्दर और दार्शनिक रूप से गहन विशेषण। अर्थ: ब्रह्म वह एक द्रष्टा (ऋषि) है जो सब आँखों से देखता है, सब मनों से सोचता है — हर जीव में, हर लोक में — देखने का हर कार्य अन्ततः उसी एक द्रष्टा का, एक विशिष्ट खिड़की से, देखना है। दो पक्षियों से सम्बन्ध: 3.1.1 का 'देखने वाला पक्षी' (अभिचाकशीति) = एकर्षि — वह एक द्रष्टा जो बिना खाए सब देखता है। अनुष्ठान-आयाम: 'स्वयं जुह्वतः एकर्षिम्' — वे स्वयं एक द्रष्टा को आहुति देते हैं — सच्ची आहुति = घी-अग्नि नहीं, स्वयं (svayam) को एक चेतना (ब्रह्म) को अर्पित करना। व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ: हर क्षण एक द्रष्टा आपको देख रहा है — यह निगरानी नहीं, अन्तरंगता है — वह द्रष्टा आपकी गहनतम प्रकृति में आप ही हैं — एकर्षि = वही दूसरा पक्षी — अनन्त धैर्य और प्रेम से सदा देखता हुआ।

Eng: The epithet 'eka-ṛṣim' ('the one Seer') is a beautiful and philosophically profound description of Brahman: What it means: Brahman is the one Seer (ṛṣi) who sees through all eyes, thinks through all minds, perceives through all consciousness. Every act of seeing — by every being, in every world — is ultimately an act of the ONE Seer seeing through a particular window. The connection to the two birds: the 'watching bird' (abhicākaśīti) of 3.1.1 is the eka-ṛṣi — the one Seer who watches everything without eating. Every being has this Seer within — it is the witness-consciousness (sākṣin) that underlies all individual awareness. The ritual dimension: 'svayaṁ juhvataḥ eka-ṛṣim' — 'they themselves offer oblations to the one Seer.' This transforms the Vedic ritual: the true oblation is not butter into fire but the offering of oneself (svayam) to the one Seer (Brahman). Every ritual, properly understood, is an offering to the one consciousness that sees through all. The practical implication: in every moment, you are being seen — by the one Seer, the ultimate witness. This isn't surveillance; it's intimacy. The Seer is not judging you — it is YOU, in your deepest nature. The eka-ṛṣi is the second bird on the tree — your own highest Self, watching, always watching, with infinite patience and love.
